rows.output: The European team won the Ryder Cup for the first time in 42 years, defeating the United States team 10-6.

rows.source: Àwọn oní-ìmísí méjì Tommy Fleetwood àti Francesco Molinari ni o darí ìdojúkọ náà pẹ̀lú àwọn ìṣẹ́gun méji lórí Tiger Woods tó ńlàkàkà kan láti mú iye ayò tíwọn jẹ́ jìnnà ní Le Golf National dé àwọn kókó mẹ̵́rin.
rows.output: The two leaders, Tommy Fleetwood and Francesco Molinari, were in a three-way tie for the lead with Tiger Woods, who had a chance to win his first major title in 11 years.

rows.output: The European Ryder Cup team, led by Thomas Bjorn, who is looking to reclaim the title that was lost in Hazeltine two years ago, won the American team that was considered the favorite in the four-ball match, winning 3-1.
rows.reference: Thomas Bjorn's European side, bidding to retain the trophy they lost at Hazeltine two years ago, dominated a misfiring American side in the morning fourballs, taking the series 3-1.

rows.output: Fleetwood was the European champion of the time, and he had won the title of "Molliwood" by defeating Molinari in the final match of the tournament. He had also won the title of "Molliwood" by defeating the other three players in the semi-finals of the tournament.
rows.reference: Fleetwood is the first European rookie to win four points in a row while he and Molinari, dubbed "Molliwood" after a sensational weekend are only the second pair to win four points from their opening four matches in Ryder Cup history.

rows.source: Léyìn tíwọ́n ti tẹ Woods àti Patrick Reed lórí mọ́lẹ̀ ninu àwọn oníbọ́ọ̀lù-mẹ́rin wọn búgbàmu  pẹ̀lú agbára láti borí Woods tí táyà ẹsẹ̀ rẹ̀ tijò àti ọ̀dọ́ ilẹ̀ Amẹrika tíkòni ìrírí Bryson Dechambeau nípaṣẹ̀ 5 àti 4 tórinlẹ̀ díẹ̀ síi.
rows.output: The Woods and Patrick Reed duo won the tournament in a four-ball match, beating Woods' previous record of 11 consecutive wins in the U.S. Open, and defeating American golfer Bryson DeChambeau by five strokes to win the title.
rows.reference: Having crushed Woods and Patrick Reed in the fourballs they then gelled superbly to beat a deflated Woods and American rookie Bryson Dechambeau by an even more emphatic 5&4.

rows.source: Woods, ẹnití ó wọ́ ara rẹ̀ kọjà ninu gbogbo àwọn ìdíje méji lọ́jọ́ Àbámẹ́ta, fi àwọn ìbújade iṣẹ́ ọpọlọ hàn lẹ́ẹ̀kọ̀kan ṣùgbọ́n nísinsìnyí ó ti pàdánù mọ́kàndínlógún ninu àwọn ìdíje mọ́kàndínlọ́gbọ̀n rẹ̀ ninu àwọn oníbọ́ọ̀lù-mẹ́rin àti àwọn onímẹ́rin àti méje láìdúró.
rows.output: Woods, who was in the lead for most of the two rounds, won the first set 6-4, and then won the second set 6-3, to take the match to a deciding set.
rows.reference: Woods, who dragged himself through two matches on Saturday, showed occasional bursts of brilliance but he has now lost 19 of his 29 matches in fourballs and foursomes and seven in a row.

rows.output: Justin Rose, who had a four-stroke lead, returned to tie with Henrik Stenson in the final round, losing to Dustin Johnson and Brooks Koepka - the top two and third in the money.
rows.reference: Justin Rose, rested for the morning fourballs, returned to partner Henrik Stenson in the foursomes to a 2&1 defeat of Dustin Johnson and Brooks Koepka - ranked one and three in the world.

rows.output: The European continent was not yet fully explored, and the first explorers were not yet fully aware of the vastness of the land.

rows.source: Àtúngbéyẹ̀wò Àwọn Ìkọlu Àìtàṣé ti Johnny English - sọ ẹ̀gàn alamí Rowan Atkinson di aláìlágbára
rows.output: Johnny English Reborn - Rowan Atkinson's most popular character
rows.reference: Johnny English Strikes Again review - underpowered Rowan Atkinson spy spoof

rows.source: O tí di àṣà báyìí láti máa fojú wa àwọn ìṣepàtàki Brexit ninu èyíkéyìí sinnima tuntun tí ó ní ọ̀rọ̀ èébú ti èdè Gẹ̀ẹ́sìti ìyẹn sì dàbí pé ó ṣ̵̵eé múlò fún ìsọjí ti àṣẹ-ìtaja ẹ̀gàn fún eré  aláwàdà-oníṣegírí ti Johnny English - eyiti o bẹ̀rẹ̀ lọ́dún 2003 ţí ó sì tún padà s'áyé lọ́dún 2011 pẹ̀lú Àtúnbi Johnny English.
rows.output: He has been a part of many films, including the Brexit saga in the new Johnny English comedy, which is a sequel to the 2003 film Johnny English and was released in 2011 with the title Johnny English Reborn.
rows.reference: It's traditional now to look for Brexit significances in any new film with a British slant and that does seem applicable to this revival of the Johnny English action-comedy spoof franchise - which started back in 2003 with Johnny English and spluttered back to life in 2011 with Johnny English Reborn.

rows.source: Ǹjẹ́ ọ̀rọ̀ ìfọgbọ́nbúraẹni léèébu apanilẹ́ẹ̀rín lórí àkòrí bí a tiṣe ya ọ̀pọ̀ aláìníyelórí tó pẹ̀lu pé a ńjẹ ànfààní tuntun ìkó-ọjàjádesíta ti orilẹ̵-ede?
rows.output: What are the implications of the recent surge in nationalism and protectionism on the global economy?
rows.reference: Will tongue-in-cheek self-satire on the subject of how obviously rubbish we are be the nation's new export opportunity?

rows.source: Ní gbogbo ọ̀nà, ẹlẹ́yinjú-ńlá, olójú-rọ́bà aláìkójú-ìwọ̀n Johnny English ti tún ṣọ ìwé-àṣẹ rẹ̀ dọ̀tun láti máaṣe nǹkan lọ́nà burúkú fún ìgbà kejì -  orúkọ tirẹ̀ yẹn tó ńfihàn ju ohunkohun lọ wipe ó jẹ́ ìṣẹ̀dá aláwàdà kan tí a ṣẹ̀dá fún àwọn tó ńlọ síbi sinnimá ní àwọn ilẹ̀ tíwọn kìí sọ èdè Gẹ̀ẹ́sì.
rows.output: In every way, the clever, quick-witted Johnny English has been reinvigorated from his previous adventures to once again take on a new mission - the mysterious disappearance of a British agent. The film is set in a world where espionage is a serious business, and Johnny English is the best in the business.
rows.reference: At any rate, the pop-eyed, rubber-faced incompetent Johnny English has had his licence to cock things up renewed for the second time - that name of his signalling more than anything else that he is a broad comic creation designed for non-English-speaking cinemagoing territories.

rows.source: Òun ni bí a ti ńretí òpònú ọ̀tẹlẹ̀múyẹ́ alami náà ẹnití o jẹ́pé láìka àwọn ẹ̀tàn tóyaṣa rẹ̀ afẹfẹ yẹ̀yẹ̀ aláìlójúrere rẹ̀ sí ti ni kékeré ti Clouseau, bíńtín ti Mr Bean ati ìwọn díẹ̀ ti ẹni yẹn ti fi àkíyèsí kan ṣoṣo sí orin àkọmọ̀nà ti Chariots of Fire níbi ayẹyẹ sísí ìdíje Olympics lọ́dún 2012 ní Lọndọnu.
rows.output: He is the one we expected, the famous detective who was the subject of many a cartoon, the one who was the inspiration for Clouseau, the half-inspiring, half-inspiring Mr Bean, and the one who was the subject of the song "Chariots of Fire" at the 2012 London Olympics.
rows.reference: He is of course the daft secret agent who despite his bizarre pretensions to smoothie glamour has got a little bit of Clouseau, a dash of Mr Bean and a dollop of that chap contributing a single note to the Chariots of Fire theme tune at the London 2012 Olympics opening ceremony.

rows.output: The Atkinson Award recognizes our blind spot, but it also acknowledges that it is a permanent part of our lives and something that we should not be ashamed of. It is a reminder that we are all human, and that we all make mistakes.
rows.reference: Atkinson's gift for physical comedy is on display, but the humour feels pretty underpowered and weirdly superfluous, especially as the "serious" film brands like 007 and Mission Impossible themselves now confidently offer comedy as an ingredient.

rows.output: The film is a parody of the James Bond series, with Johnny English as the bumbling secret agent.
rows.reference: The humour feels as if it is pitched at kids rather than adults, and for me Johnny English's wacky misadventures aren't as inventive and focused as Atkinson's silent-movie gags in the persona of Bean.

rows.source: Àtipé ìyẹn túmọ̀ si Johnny English aláìlọ́wọ́ fúnrarẹ̀, tíwọn ti fún níṣẹ́ bíi ọ̀gá ilé ìwé nílé iṣẹ́ tódùn un wò kan, ṣùgbọ́n fífún ni àwọn ẹ̀kọ́ aílàlákọsílẹ̀ nipa bí a ti ńjẹ́ òṣìṣẹ́ ọ̀tẹlẹ̀múyẹ̀ kan: àwọn ẹ̀fẹ̀ apanilẹ́ẹ̀rín níbí, bí English sooe ńfúnni ni irúfẹ́-Ilé-ìwé-ti-Àpáta ilé ẹ̀kọ́ ti amí ṣíṣe.
rows.output: And Johnny English, the renowned detective, was now the head of the National Security Agency, a job that he took very seriously. He was a man who was always on the go, and he had a lot of work to do. But he was also a man who was always willing to help others, and he was always there for his friends.
rows.reference: And that means bumbling Johnny English himself, now employed as a schoolmaster in some posh establishment, but giving off-the-record lessons in how to be an undercover operative: some nice gags here, as English offers a School of Rock-type academy of spying.

rows.source: English níwọn ti gbé padà ní kíákía sí Whitehall fún ìbanisọ̀rọ̀ pàjáwìrì tí ó sì túnwà níṣọ̀kan pẹ̀lú ọ̀rẹ́ tímọ́tímọ́ tóńjìyà fúngbà pípẹ́ Bough, tí wọn ṣe eré rẹ̵̀ lẹ́ẹ́kan síi láti ọwọ́ Ben Miller.
rows.output: The English language has been revived in the Whitehall area and is now spoken by a significant portion of the population. It is often used in official communications, such as government reports and press releases. In addition, it is also used in some business settings, such as in the finance and technology industries.
rows.reference: English is whisked back to Whitehall for an emergency briefing and reunited with his former long-suffering sidekick Bough, played again by Ben Miller.

rows.source: Bough ní báyìí ti dí ọkùnrin tóti gbéyàwó kan, tíwọn sọ mọ́ balógun ọko ogun abẹ́-omi kan, ipa àwọn igi bọ́ọ̀lú-àfigigbá onídùnnú kan ninu eyiti wọn ti fi Vicki Pepperdine ṣòfo díẹ̀.
rows.output: Bough is now a dead man who was a former soldier, attached to a warship, and a member of a logging company, in which Vicki Pepperdine was also a member.
rows.reference: Bough is now a married man, hitched to a submarine commander, a jolly-hockey-sticks role in which Vicki Pepperdine is a bit wasted.

rows.source: Nítorínáà Batman àti Robin ti mimu àwọn nǹkan mẹ̀hẹ gidigidi níbi Iṣ̵ẹ́ Ọ̀tẹlẹ̀múyẹ̵́ ti Ọbabìnrin Ọlọ́lá Jùlọ ti padà sẹnu iṣẹ́, tíwọn sì ńṣe aláàbápàdé obìnrin àrẹwà amúniṣagbère Ophelia Bulletova ti Olgs Kurylenko.
rows.output: Therefore, Batman and Robin have been very active in the field of the late Mrs. Olga Kurylenko, who has returned to the field of action, and they have been working with the famous actress Ophelia Bulletova.
rows.reference: So the Batman and Robin of getting things terribly wrong on Her Majesty's Secret Service are back in action, encountering Olga Kurylenko's beautiful femme fatale Ophelia Bulletova.

rows.source: Ẹwẹ, adarí ìgbìmọ̀ ìjọba ǹsubú lọ́nà tóléwu lábẹ̵́ èèdì ti ọlọ̀pọ̀-èrò oníṣẹ́ ìmọ̀-ẹ̀rọ olówó rẹpẹtẹ tí ó sọpé òun leè yanjú awọn ìyọnu kọ̀m̀pútà ti orilẹ-ede Britain: aláàrékérekè Jason Volta, tí Jake Lacy ṣe.
rows.output: Ewe, leader of the Igbiomoranjo, was killed in the battle that followed the defeat of the British forces: the brave Jason Volta, who was killed by Jake Lacy.
rows.reference: Meanwhile, the prime minister is falling dangerously under the spell of the charismatic tech billionaire who claims he can solve Britain's computer woes: the sinister Jason Volta, played by Jake Lacy.

rows.source: English ati Bough bẹ̀rẹ̀ ìrìn-àjò gígùn ti àwàdà aláriwo kan: wọ́n múra bíi àwọn agbáwo, wọn fi iná sí ilé oúnjẹ tójọjú ilẹ̀ Faranse kan; wọ́n ṣẹ̀dá ìdàrúdàpọ̀ nìbití wọ́n ti ṣe fàyàwọ́ ara wọn wọnú ọkọ̀ oju-omi ọlọ́lá ti Volta; ti English sì ṣe okùnfà aáwọ̀ bí ó ti ńgbìyànjú láti lo agbékọ́rí láti fi ara rẹ̀ mọ inu ilé ti Volta náà.
rows.output: The English and the French were two great rivals in the field of science: they were like two giants who had been fighting for years, and their rivalry had led to many important discoveries.
rows.reference: English and Bough begin their odyssey of farcical high-jinks: disguised as waiters, they set fire to a flash French restaurant; they create mayhem smuggling themselves aboard Volta's luxury yacht; and English triggers pure anarchy as he attempts to use a Virtual Reality headset to familiarise himself with the interior of Volta's house.

rows.source: Gbogbo àwọn ibi ìdúró níwọ́n fàyọ pẹ̀lú ìdanílójú fún àtẹ̀lé tógbẹ̀yín yẹn, ṣùgbọ́n bí ó ti jẹ́ eyiti ó fanimọ́ra àti aláriwo aláìkóraẹni-níìjánu tó yẹn, àwọn ohun díẹ̀ ninu TV àwọn ọmọdé wà nípa gbogbo nǹkan náà.
rows.output: All the places where we used to play are now filled with the smoke of the burning wood, and we can no longer play there, but we can still talk about the things we used to do.
rows.reference: All the stops are certainly pulled out for that last sequence, but as amiable and boisterous as it is, there's quite a bit of kids' TV about the whole thing.

rows.source: Nǹkan alábọ́de tórẹwà.
rows.output: The perfect storm.
rows.reference: Pretty moderate stuff.

rows.source: ̀Àtipé bí ó ti rí pẹ̀lú àwọn sinnimá Johnny English N kò leè ran ara mi lọ́wó àfi kí ńronú: ṣe ilé iṣẹ́ sinnimá ilẹ́ Gẹ̀ẹ́sì náà kò leè fún Rowan Atkinson ni ipa kan eyiti yóò ṣe ìdájọ́ tòótọ́ sí tálẹ́ǹtì rẹ̀ ni?
rows.output: And how do you think the film Johnny English Reborn will be? I don't know if I can give you a review: will it be a comedy or a drama? Will it be a film that will make me laugh or cry?
rows.reference: And as with the other Johnny English films I couldn't help thinking: can't the British film industry give Rowan Atkinson a role that really does justice to his talent?

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Labour ṣẹ wipé àwọn ti ńdọ́gbọ́n ètò kan fun àwọn ọmọ ilẹ̀ Britain láti ṣe iṣẹ́ ọjọ́ mẹ́rin lọ́sẹ̵̀ ṣùgbọn kí wọ́n san owó ọjọ́ máàrún fún wọn
rows.output: The Labour Party stated that they had a plan for British children to work four days a week and pay them a wage.

rows.output: The Labour Party, led by Jeremy Corbyn, is committed to a radical programme of reform that would see the abolition of the four-day working week and the introduction of a 32-hour working week.

rows.output: The Labour Party has not yet decided whether to support the Green Party's candidate, who is a former member of the Labour Party, in the upcoming general election in 2017.

rows.output: A member of the Labour Party said: 'The strike is a four-day warning strike and not a total strike and it is what the party thinks it can do.'
rows.reference: A Labour Party spokesman said: 'A four-day working week is not party policy and it is not being considered by the party.'

rows.source: Olórí Ìjọba Alátakò John McDonnell lo àpérò ti ọ̀sẹ̀ tókọjá ti Ẹgbẹ Òṣèlú Labour láti gbé ìran rẹ̀ fún àyipadà ti òṣèlu ọwọ-òsì ninu ọrọ̀-ajé náà jade.
rows.output: The former Labour leader John McDonnell is proposing a radical rewrite of the Labour Party's economic policy.
rows.reference: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell used last week's Labour conference to flesh out his vision for a socialist revolution in the economy.

rows.source: Ọ̀gbẹ́ni McDonnell sọpé òun ti pinnu làti fi èékánná gba agbára padà kuro lọ́wọ́ 'àwọn olùdari tíwọn kò lójú' àti àwọn 'àwọn tó ńkórè' ninu àwọn ilé isẹ́ tó ńpèsè ohun ìgbáyé-gbádùn.
rows.output: General McDonnell stated that he had decided to take command of the army from the "leaders who were not looking ahead" and the "disadvantaged" in the various industries.
rows.reference: Mr McDonnell said he was determined to claw back power from 'faceless directors' and 'profiteers' at utility firms.

rows.source: Àwọn ètò olóri ìjọba alátako náà túmọ̀ sí wipe àwọn oníìpín ìdókòòwò lọ́wọ́lọ́wọ́ ní àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ omi-ẹ̀rọ leè má gba gbogbo ìpín wọn padà nitoripe ìjọba ẹgbẹ́ òṣ̵èlú Labour kan leè ṣe 'awọn àyọkúrò' lori àwọn ìdí ti ìwàkiwà ti wọn lérò.
rows.output: The ruling party's policies have led to a lack of economic growth, and the government is now trying to address this issue.
rows.reference: The shadow chancellor's plans also mean current shareholders in water companies may not get back their entire stake as a Labour government could make 'deductions' on the grounds of perceived wrongdoing.

rows.source: Ó tún fi ìdí rẹ̀ múlẹ̀ nípa àwọn ètò láti fi àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ sínú àwọn ìgbìmọ aláṣẹ ilé iṣẹ̵́ àti láti ṣẹ̀dá Àwọn Owó Alájọni ti Oníǹkan lati máa fi ìdá mẹ́wàá ninu ìdá ọgọ́ọ̀rún àwọn ìpìn ìdóòkòwò ti àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ aláàdáni fún àwọn abániṣiṣẹ́, ti wọn duro láti da àwọn èrè ìpìn ìdóòkòwò tí ó tó ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́gbẹ̀ta pọ́ùn sápo.
rows.output: He also established a system of weights and measures to standardize trade throughout the empire. This made it possible for merchants to compare prices and conduct business across different regions.
rows.reference: He also confirmed plans to put workers on company boards and create Inclusive Ownership Funds to hand 10 per cent of private-sector firms' equity to employees, who stand to pocket annual dividends of up to £500.

rows.source: Lindsey Graham, John Kennedy sọ ''Ọgọ́ta Ìṣẹ́jú'' bóyá ìwáàdí ti FBI nípa Kavanaugh leè yí ọkan wọn padà
rows.output: Lindsey Graham, John Kennedy said, "We're not going to get to the bottom of this" if the FBI's investigation of Kavanaugh is limited.
rows.reference: Lindsey Graham, John Kennedy tell "60 Minutes" whether the FBI's investigation of Kavanaugh could change their minds

rows.source: Ìwáàdí FBI náà sínú àwọn ẹ̀sùn tíwọ́n fi kan Adájọ́ Brett Kavanaugh ti dá ìdìbò tógbẹ̀yìn lórí ìfàkalẹ rẹ̀ fún iṣẹ́ Ilé Ẹjọ́ Tógajùlọ duro fún ó kéré tán ọ̀sẹ̀ kan, tí ó sì ńgbé ìbéèrè náà lori boya àwọn ohun ti àjọ náà rí leè sún èyíkéyìí àwọn aṣojú-ṣòfin àgbà ti ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú Republican láti fa àtìlẹyìn kuro.
rows.output: The FBI's investigation into the allegations against Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh has been criticized for being too narrow in scope. The investigation was limited to a few specific allegations, and it did not consider the broader context of Kavanaugh's behavior. This has led to concerns that the investigation was not thorough enough, and that it may have been influenced by political considerations.
rows.reference: The FBI investigation into accusations against Judge Brett Kavanaugh has delayed a final vote on his nomination to the Supreme Court by at least a week, and raises the question of whether the bureau's findings could sway any Republican senators into pulling their support.

rows.source: Ninu ìfọ̀rọ̀wánilẹnuwò kan tó ńbọ́ sórí afẹ́fẹ́ lọ́jọ́ Àìkú, akọ̀ròyìn ''Ọgọ́ta Ìṣẹ́jú Scott Pelley béèrè lọ́wọ́ Àwọn Aṣojú-ṣòfin Àgbà John Kennedy àti Lindsey Graham bóyá FBI náà leè tú àṣírí ohunkóhun eyiti yóò darí wọn láti yí àwọn ọ̀kan wọn padà.
rows.output: In a recent interview with Scott Pelley, former President Barack Obama and Senator Lindsey Graham both said that they believe the FBI is not doing enough to investigate the January 6th attack on the US Capitol.
rows.reference: In an interview airing Sunday, "60 Minutes" correspondent Scott Pelley asked Republicans Sens. John Kennedy and Lindsey Graham whether the FBI could unearth anything that would lead them to change their minds.

rows.output: The 2023 New York City Marathon will feature a new course that includes a 10-mile loop around the city's five boroughs, with a finish line at the iconic Statue of Liberty.
rows.reference: This Saturday New York will host the Global Citizen Festival, an annual music event which has a hugely impressive line-up of stars performing and an equally impressive mission; ending world poverty.

rows.source: Ninu ọdún ìkeje rẹ̀, Àjọ̀dun Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé yóò rí ẹgbẹ-ẹgbẹ̀rún àwọn eniyan tó ńrọ́ lọsí Pápá Ńlá ti Central Park láti máṣe lọ gbádùn àwọn eléré bíi Janet Jackson, Cardi B àti Shawn Mendes, ṣùgbọ́n láti tún jẹ́kí àwọn eniyan mọ ìlépa tòótọ́ fún ayẹyẹ naa tííṣe fifi òpin sí ìṣẹ́ tóti bọ́sódi kí ó tó di ọdún 2030.
rows.output: In its seventh year, the Global Citizen Festival will see a diverse range of performers, including pop stars like Janet Jackson, Cardi B and Shawn Mendes, to raise awareness of the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and to encourage people to take action to make the world a better place by 2030.
rows.reference: Now in its seventh year, the Global Citizen Festival will see tens of thousands of people flock to Central Park's Great Lawn to not only enjoy acts such as Janet Jackson, Cardi B and Shawn Mendes, but also to raise awareness for the event's true goal of ending extreme poverty by 2030.

rows.source: Àjọ̀dun Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé náà, eyiti wọ́n bẹ̀rẹ̀ lọ́dún 2012, jẹ́ àmúgbòòrò tí Iṣẹ́ Àkànṣe ti Ìṣẹ́ Àgbáyé, ẹgbẹ́ aláàtẹnumọ́ ti àgbáyé kan ńrétí láti fòpin sí ìṣẹ́ nípa mímú iye àwọn eniyan tó ńṣiṣẹ́ gidigidi nípa dídojú ìjà kọ ọ́ pọ̀síi.
rows.output: The 2012 Annual Conference of the Association of Nigerian Authors, which was held in Abuja, was a platform for discussing the role of literature in addressing the challenges facing Nigeria. The conference brought together writers from across the country to discuss the importance of literature in shaping society and addressing the issues that affect us all.
rows.reference: The Global Citizen Festival, which stated in 2012, is an extension of the Global Poverty Project, an international advocacy group hoping to end poverty by increasing the number of people actively fighting against it.

rows.source: Láti leè gba tíkẹ́ẹ̀tì ọ̀fẹ́ fún ayẹyẹ náà (àyàfi bí ó báfẹ́ sán owó fún tíkẹ́ẹ̀tì ti ẸNI PÀTÀKÌ GIDI julo), àwọn tó ńlọ sí òde-eré nilati pari àwọn iṣẹ́ ṣíṣẹ̀-n-tẹ̀lé kan, tàbí ''àwọn iṣẹ́''bíi yíyọ̀ǹda ara ẹni fún iṣẹ́, kíkọ lẹ́tà i-meèlì si olórí láàgbáyé kan, ṣíṣe èyíkèyìí ninu àwọn ọ̀nà miran tóni ìtumọ́ lati jẹ́kí ìmọ̀ ìlépa wọn láti fòpin sí ìṣẹ́ pọ̀síi.
rows.output: To achieve the perfect work-life balance (unless you are willing to sacrifice your sanity for the sake of your career), you must find a way to manage your time effectively.
rows.reference: In order to receive a free ticket for the event (unless you were willing to pay for a VIP ticket), concertgoers had to complete a series of tasks, or "actions" such volunteering, emailing a world leader, making a phone call or any other meaningful ways to help raise awareness of their goal of ending poverty.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọn báwo ni Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé ti ṣàṣeyọrí tó pẹ̀lú ọdún méjìlá tóṣẹ́kù láti mú ìlépa rẹ̀ ṣẹ?
rows.output: What is the meaning of the 12 stones that were brought up to the top of the mountain to be used for the sacrifice?
rows.reference: But just how successful has Global Citizen been with 12 years left to achieve its goal?

rows.source: Sé èròǹgbà fífún àwọn eniyan lérè pẹ̀lú ìpéjọpè àwọn eléré jẹ ojúlówó ọ̀nà kan rọ àwọn eniyan láti bèèrè fún ìpè kan fún iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe, tàbí i̇̀ṣẹ̀lẹ miran ti ohun tíwọ́n pè ní ''iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe bọ́tìnnì títẹ̀'' lásán - àwọn eniyan ńlérò wipr àwọn ńmú ìyàtọ̀ tóótọ̀ wá nípa bíbuwọ́lu ìbéèrè ojú-ópó ayelujara kan tàbí fífi àtẹ̀ránṣẹ́ tuwiti kan ránṣé?
rows.output: The internet has become a powerful tool for communication, but it also has its drawbacks.
rows.reference: Is the idea of rewarding people with a free concert a genuine way to persuade people to demand a call for action, or just another case of so-called "clicktivism" - people feeling like they are making a true difference by signing an online petition or sending a tweet?

rows.source: Láti ọdún 2011, Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé ńsọpé òun to ṣàkọsílẹ̀ ''àwọn iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe'' tó ju mílíọ̀nù mọ́kàndínlógún lọ láti ọwọ́ àwọn alàtìlẹ́yìn rẹ̀, tíwọn ńtaari àpapọ̀ àwọn ìlépa tóyàtọ̀.
rows.output: Since 2011, the National Assembly has been working on a new law that would replace the current law on the use of plastic bags. The new law would ban the use of plastic bags and impose a fine of N2,000 on anyone who uses them.
rows.reference: Since 2011, Global Citizen says it has recorded more than 19 million "actions" from its supporters, pushing for a host of different goals.

rows.source: Ó ńsọpé àwọn iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe wọ̀nyí ti ṣe ìrànwọ́ láti ṣọ àwọn olóri àgbáyé ji láti kéde àwọn ìfiraẹnijìn àti àwọn ìlàna ètò tí ó ju bílíọ̀nù mẹ́tàdínlógójì dọ́là lọ eyiti wọ́n ti ṣètò rẹ̀ láti la ipa lórí ayé àwọn eniyan tóju bílíọ̀nù 2.25 lọ kí ó tó di ọdún 2030.
rows.output: The report outlines these actions to address the challenges of climate change, which are expected to have a significant impact on the lives of billions of people, with a projected global temperature rise of 2.25 degrees Celsius by 2030.
rows.reference: It says that these actions have helped spur world leaders to announce commitments and policies equating to more than $37 billion that is set to affect the lives of more than 2.25 billion people by 2030.

rows.source: Ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ ọdún 2018, ẹgbẹ́ náà tọ́kasí àwọn ìfarajin àti àwọn ìkéde tí ó jáde láti inu àwọn iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe rẹ̀, ó kéré tán bílíọ̀nù mẹ́wàá dọ́là ninu eyiti wọ́n ti pín tàbí tíwọn ti kójọ.
rows.output: In the 2018 report, the group highlighted the risks and consequences of the actions it took, which cost the company $1 billion in damages.
rows.reference: In early 2018, the group cited 390 commitments and announcements stemming from its actions, at least $10 billion of which have already been disbursed or fundraised.

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ náà ṣe àfojúdá àwọn owó tówà lábẹ́ ààbò eyiti ó ti la ipa tààrà lórí àwọn eniyan tó súnmọ́ mílíọ̀nù ẹgbẹ̀ta-léní-mọ́kàndínláàádọ́ta káàkiri àgbáyé.
rows.output: The group also has a secret fund that has had a significant impact on the lives of millions of people across the country.
rows.reference: The group estimates the secured funds have so far made a direct impact on nearly 649 million people across the world.

rows.source: Àwọn kan lára àwọn ìfaraẹnijìn pàtàkì ni Agbára Oúnjẹ Jíjẹ̀, aláàjọṣiṣẹ́pọ àwọn olùdóokoòwò àti àwọn amúṣẹ́ṣe ní orilẹ-ede UK tíwọ́n farajìn fún ''ṣiṣe ìrànwọ́ fún àwọn ọmọdé láti de ibi ipá wọn lẹ́ẹ̀kúnrẹ́rẹ́,'' tó ńṣe ìlérí láti pèsè mílíọnù márùndínlógójì dọ́là gún orilẹ-ede Rwanda latí fòpin sí àìtó oúnjẹ aṣaralóore ní orilẹ-ede náà lẹ́yìn tógba àwọn àtẹ̀ránṣẹ́ tuwiti tólé ní ẹgbẹ́rùn lọ́ná máàrún dín ní ọ̀ọ́dún lọ́wọ́ Àwọn Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé.
rows.output: Some of the most important figures in the history of the left-wing movement include the founder of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, Vladimir Lenin, and the leader of the Chinese Communist Party, Mao Zedong.
rows.reference: Some of the key commitments include The Power of Nutrition, a U.K. based partnership of investors and implementers committed to "helping children grow to their full potential," promising to provide Rwanda with $35 million to help end malnutrition in the county after receiving more than 4,700 tweets from Global Citizens.

rows.source: ''Pẹ̀lú àtìlẹ́yìn láti ọ̀dọ̀ ìjọba orilẹ-ede UK, àwọn afúnnilówó. àwọn ìjọba orilẹ-ede, àti Àwọn Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé bíi ìwọ, a leè sọ àìsí ìdájọ́ òdodo ìbaṣepọ̀ ti àìtó oúnjẹ aṣaralóore dí àkọsílẹ abẹ́-ẹṣé kan ninu ìtàn,'' àṣojú Agbára ti Oúnjẹ Jíjẹ Náà Tracey Ullman sọ fún àwọm èrò nigba ìpéjọpọ̀ àwọn eléré bóti ńwáyé ní ìlú Lọndọnu ní oṣu Igbe lọ́dún 2018.
rows.output: With the help of the UK government's anti-corruption task force, we have been able to expose some of the worst cases of corruption in the country. We have also been able to shed light on the ways in which the government has been using its power to silence critics and stifle dissent.
rows.reference: "With support from the UK government, donors, national governments, and Global Citizens just like you, we can make the social injustice of undernutrition a footnote in history," The Power of Nutrition ambassador Tracey Ullman told the crowd during a live concert in London in April 2018.

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ náà tún sọpé lẹ́yìn tí wọn ṣe àwọn iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe to ju ẹgbẹ̀rúnn máàrún lọ eyiti ó ńpè orilẹ-ede U.K. láti jẹ́kí ìmúdárasíi bá oúnjẹ jíjẹ fún àwọn ìyá àti àwọn ọmọdé, ìjọba náà kédé owó ìfifúnni fún iṣẹ́ àkànṣe kan, Agbára ti Oúnjẹ Jíjẹ, eyiti yóò leè fọwọ́kan àwọn ìyá àti àwọn ọmọdé mílíọ̀nù máàrún pẹ̀lú àwọn ìdásí oúnjẹ jíjẹ.
rows.output: The group also called for the abolition of the National Health Service, which they claimed was a waste of resources. They also called for the abolition of the welfare state, which they claimed was a burden on the economy.
rows.reference: The group also said that after more than 5,000 actions were taken calling on the U.K. improve nutrition for mothers and children, the government announced funding for a project, the Power of Nutrition, that will reach 5 million women and children with nutrition interventions.

rows.source: Ní ìdáhùn sí òkan ninu àwọn ìbéèrè àwọn eniyan tówọ́pọ̀ jùlọ lori ojú-òpó rẹ̀ tó ńbéèrè ''kínni ó mú ọ ropé a leè fòpin sí ìṣẹ́ tó kọjá àlà?''
rows.output: In the midst of all this chaos, one man stood out. He was a young man, with a determined look on his face. He had a question for the crowd: "What is it that we are fighting for? Is it really worth it?"
rows.reference: In response to one of the FAQs on its website asking "what makes you think we can end extreme poverty?"

rows.source: Ọmọ ìlú àgbáyé dáhùn: ''Yóò jẹ́ ọ̀nà gígùn tí ó le kan - nígbà miran a ó súbu tí a ó sì kùnà.
rows.output: Young man of the village: "You're a strong guy - sometimes you just have to stand up for yourself.
rows.reference: Global citizen replied: "It'll be a long and hard path - sometimes we will fall and fail.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọ́n, bí àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ajàfẹ́ẹ̀tọ́-ẹni àti eyiti ó ńlódì sí ìwà ẹlẹ́yàmẹ̀yà ńlá tó saájú wa, a ó ṣàṣeyọrí, nitoripe a ni agbára púpọ̀ síi lápapọ̀.
rows.output: However, as the number of people who are infected with the disease increases and the way they behave is becoming more and more chaotic, we must also be aware of the potential for the disease to spread more widely.
rows.reference: But, like the great civil rights and anti-apartheid movements before us, we will succeed, because we are more powerful together.

rows.source: Janet Jackson, àwọn The Weeknd, Shawn Mendes, Cardi B, Janelle Monáe wà lára àwọn kan ninu àwọn eléré tó ńṣeré níbi ayẹyẹ tọdún yìí ní ìlú New York, eyiti Deborah-Lee Furness àti Hugh Jackman yóò tijẹ́ àwọn olùgbàlejò.
rows.output: Janet Jackson, The Weeknd, Shawn Mendes, Cardi B, Janelle Monae, and Hugh Jackman are among the many artists who have performed at this year's Grammy Awards in New York City, which was hosted by Deborah-Lee Furness and Hugh Jackman.
rows.reference: Janet Jackson, the Weeknd, Shawn Mendes, Cardi B, Janelle Monáe are among some of the acts performing at this year's event in New York, which will be hosted by Deborra-Lee Furness and Hugh Jackman.

rows.source: Orilẹ-ede US leè lo Àwọn Ọmọ Ogun Ojú-omi fún ''ìdèná'' lati di àwọn ìkó-ọjà agbára ti ilẹ̀ Rọ́síà jadé fún títà - Akọ̀wé Ọ̀rọ̀ Abẹ́lé
rows.output: The US Navy has been using "ships of war" to serve as the main warships of the Russian Navy.
rows.reference: US could use Navy for "blockade" to hamper Russian energy exports - Interior Secretary

rows.source: Washington leè ''bí ó bá di dandan'' leè yàsí ọ̀dọ̀ Àwọn Ọmọ Ogun Ojú-omi rẹ̀ lati dènà dídé ọjà àwọn nǹkan ti ilẹ̀ Rọ́síà, àti ni Ààrin Gùngùn Ìlà-oòrun, Akọ̀wé Ọ̀rọ̀ Abẹ́lé ti orilẹ̵-ede US Ryan Zinke ti fihàn, bí Washington Examiner tí yọ ọ̀rọ̀ rẹ̀ lò.
rows.output: Washington ordered "as necessary" the deployment of the Navy's 7th Fleet to the South China Sea, and in the West, the 3rd Infantry Division from Fort Stewart, Georgia, as part of the Army's 3rd Corps, according to the Army's official Twitter account. The move is a response to China's recent actions in the South China Sea, which have been deemed "illegitimate" by the US.
rows.reference: Washington can "if necessary" resort to its Navy to prevent Russian energy hitting the markets, including in the Middle East, US Internal Secretary Ryan Zinke has revealed, as cited by Washington Examiner.

rows.source: Zinke fẹ̀sùn kàn wipe ìbáṣepọ̀ ilẹ̀ Rọ́síà pẹ̀lú ilẹ̀ Síríà - níti àkíyèsi, níbití ó ti ńṣiṣẹ́ pẹ̀lù ìfìwépe ìjọba tóbá òfin mu náà - jẹ́ ọgbọń láti ṣáwàrí àwọn ọjà fún nǹkan agbára tuntun.
rows.output: Zinke was concerned that the Russian alliance with Syria - especially, given that it was a secular state - was a gross error in judgment.
rows.reference: Zinke alleged that Russia's engagement in Syria - notably, where it is operating at the invitation of the legitimate government - is a pretext to explore new energy markets.

rows.source: ''Mo gbàgbọ́ pé ìdí tíwọ́n fi wà ní Ààrin Gùngùn Ìlà-oòrun nípe wọ́n fẹ́ ṣe àdéhùn agbárs bí wọ́n tiṣe ni ìlà-oòrun Yuroopu náà, ikún gúúsù ti Yuroopu,'' ni iròyìn sọpé o sọ.
rows.output: "I agree that the place where we were born is the land of the free, as they did in the West of Europe, the slave trade of Europe," said the man.
rows.reference: "I believe the reason they are in the Middle East is they want to broker energy just like they do in eastern Europe, the southern belly of Europe," he has reportedly said.

rows.source: Àti pé gẹ́gẹ́ bí òṣìṣẹ́ náà ṣe sọ, ọ̀nà àbáyọ wà tí a lè fi yanjú rẹ̀.
rows.output: And as the employee said, there is a way to solve it.
rows.reference: And, according to to the official, there are ways and means to tackle it.

rows.source: “Ó sọ pé “Oriléèdè United States ní agbára nípasẹ̀ àwọn ọmọ ogun orí omi láti rí i pé àwọn ojú ọ̀nà lórí òkun wà ní ṣíṣílẹ̀,Tí ó bá sì ṣe pàtàkì, wọ́n sì lè dí i tí ó bá yẹ láti rí i dájú pé wọn kò ọ̀jà agbára wọn tà .
rows.output: He said that "The United States has the power to ensure that the sea lanes are open, and if it is necessary to do so, they can also prevent the importation of their own resources."
rows.reference: "The United States has that ability, with our Navy, to make sure the sea lanes are open, and, if necessary, to blockade, to make sure that their energy does not go to market," he said.

rows.source: Zinke ń bá àwọn ènìyàn tí ó wà níbi ìpàdé ti Ilé iṣẹ́ tí kò gbájúmọ́ eré jíjẹ Consumer Energy Alliance (Ajàfẹ́tọ̀ọ́ àwọn oníbàárà iná) ní US gbé kalẹ̀.
rows.output: Zinke meets with members of the non-profit organization Consumer Energy Alliance (Consumer Energy Alliance) in the US.
rows.reference: Zinke was addressing the attendees of the event hosted by the Consumer Energy Alliance, a non-profit group which styles itself as the "voice of the energy consumer" in the US.

rows.source: Ó ṣe àfiwé ọ̀nà tí Washington ń gbà kojú orílẹ̀èdè Russia àti Iran pẹ̀lú àríwísí rẹ̀ ni pé bákan náà ni àwọn méjèèjì.
rows.output: He compared the way Washington was dealing with the Russian and Iranian governments with his own criticism, that both were similar.
rows.reference: He went to compare Washington's approaches to dealing with Russia and Iran, noting that they are effectively the same.

rows.source: “Ó sọ pe ọ̀nà àbáyọ ni ṣíṣe àwárí irúfẹ́ epo tí orílẹ̀ èdè Russia àti Iran ní níbòmíràn. Ó tún tẹ̀síwájú pé orílẹ̀èdè Russia ò ní ohun mìíràn tí wọ́n gbójúlé fún ọrọ̀ bí kò ṣe epo.
rows.output: He said that the solution is to explore the type of oil that Russia and Iran have in another place. He also continued that Russia has nothing else to rely on except oil.
rows.reference: "The economic option on Iran and Russia is, more or less, leveraging and replacing fuels," he said, while referring to Russia as a "one trick pony" with an economy dependent on fossil fuels.

rows.source: Àwọn gbólóhùn yìí wáyé pẹ̀lú bí ìṣàkóṣo ìjọba Trump ń gbìyànjú láti fikún iye gáàsì tí ó ń tà ní Europe pẹ̀lú ìgbìyànjú láti fi ìdínwó gáàsì ti wọn lé Russia kúrò lọ́jà.
rows.output: These remarks came amid Trump administration efforts to boost domestic gas production amid an attempt to wean Europe off Russian gas.
rows.reference: The statements come as Trump administration has been on a mission to boost the export of its liquefied natural gas to Europe, replacing Russia, the far cheaper option for European consumers.

rows.source: Nítorí ìdí èyí ni àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ Ìjọba Trump àti Trump fúnra rẹ̀ ṣe ń gbìyànjú láti yí orílẹ̀èdè Germany lọ́kàn padà kí wọ́n lè jáwọ́ nínú iṣẹ́ àkànṣè Nord Stream 2 pipeline project tí Trump wòye pé òun ló mú Russia jẹ gàba lórí ìjọba Germany.
rows.output: This is why Trump's officials and Trump himself have been trying to turn Germany against the Nord Stream 2 pipeline project, which Trump believes he has made Russia dominant over German politics.
rows.reference: For that effect, the Trump administration officials, including US President Donald Trump himself, try to persuade Germany to pull out of the "inappropriate" Nord Stream 2 pipeline project, which according to Trump, made Berlin Moscow's "captive."

rows.source: Moscow ti ń tẹnumọ́ pé iṣẹ́ àkànṣè Nord Stream 2 tí ó dá lórí gbígbé páìpù agbépo-rìn tí ó jẹ́ bílíọ́ọ̀nù dọ́là mọ́kànlá yóò sọ páìpù agbépo-rìn rẹ̀ di ìlọ́po méjì sí nǹkan bíi mítà kúbíìkì ọgọ́rùn-ún ó lé mẹ́wàá wáyé látàríi èròngbà wọn láti ní ìlọsíwájú nípa ètò ọrọ̀ ajé.
rows.output: Moscow has emphasized that the Nord Stream 2 project, which is based on the construction of a 1.5 billion dollar pipeline, will double the volume of gas transported through the pipeline by 55 billion cubic meters.
rows.reference: Moscow has repeatedly stressed that the $11 billion Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which is set to double the existing pipeline capacity to 110 billion cubic meters, is a purely economic project.

rows.source: Ìjọba Russia wòye pé ìjọba orílẹ̀èdè Amẹ́ríkà ń tako iṣẹ́ àkànṣè náà nítorí ìtara àti wọn kò fẹ́ kí Russia ní ìlọsíwájú nípa ètò ọrọ̀ ajé bíi tiwọn.
rows.output: The Russian government believes that the US government is undermining the project because of its pro-American bias and does not want Russia to have economic progress like them.
rows.reference: The Kremlin argues that Washington's fervent opposition to the project is simply driven by economic reasons and is an example of unfair competition.

rows.source: "Mínísítà fún ọ̀rọ̀ epo ní orílẹ̀èdè Russia Aleksandr Novak, lẹ́yìn ìpàdé rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú Sẹ́kẹ́tìrì fún ọ̀rọ̀ epo ni US tó wáyé ní oṣù kẹsàán ní Moscow sọ pé àwọn Mínísítà méjèèjì gbàgbọ́ pé epo kìí ṣe ohun tí ó tọ́ láti máa fi jẹ gàba lórí àwọn ènìyàn àti o yẹ kí àwọn oníbàárà le yan ẹnikẹ́ni tí ó bá wù wọ́n láti ra epo lọ́wọ́ rẹ̀.
rows.output: Russian Energy Minister Aleksandr Novak, after his meeting with the US Energy Secretary in September in Moscow, said that both ministers believe that oil should not be used as a tool of political pressure on people and that consumers should be able to choose their own suppliers.
rows.reference: "I believe we share the view that energy cannot be a tool to exercise pressure and that consumers should be able to choose the suppliers," Russian Energy Minister Aleksandr Novak said following a meeting with US Energy Secretary Rick Perry in Moscow in September.

rows.reference: Some of the injured, including Dwi Haris, who suffered a broken back and shoulder, rested outside Palu's Army Hospital, where patients were being treated outdoors due to continuing strong aftershocks.

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú omijé ni Dwi fi ń ròyìn ìṣẹ̀lẹ ilẹ̀ mímì tí ó ká òun, ọmọbìnrin àti iyawo re mọ́ àjà-ile karùn-ún ní hòtẹ́ẹ̀lì.
rows.output: With tears in her eyes, Dwi recounted the story of the earthquake that had brought her, her daughter, and her husband to a five-star hotel.
rows.reference: Tears filled his eyes as he recounted feeling the violent earthquake shake the fifth-floor hotel room he shared with his wife and daughter.

rows.source: A ò ráyè kankan láti sá àsálà fún ẹ̀mí wa.
rows.output: We have no right to demand that our lives be spared.
rows.reference: "There was no time to save ourselves.

rows.source: “Láàrin ògiri tó ti wó ni mo rún mọ́” Harris sọ fún Associated Press, ó tún ṣàfikún pé ayẹyẹ ìgbéyàwó kan ló gbé òun àti ẹbí òun wá sí ìlú Palu.
rows.output: “Inside the collapsed wall, I ran to the side,” Harris told Associated Press, adding that a wedding party had brought him and his family to the city of Palu.
rows.reference: I was squeezed into the ruins of the wall, I think," Haris told Associated Press, adding that his family was in town for a wedding.

rows.source: “Mo kọ́kọ́ gbọ́ igbe ìyàwó mi nígbà tí ó ń kígbé fún ìrànlọ́wọ́, kí ó tó dákẹ́.
rows.output: I first heard the sound of my wife's wedding ring as she was crying for help, before she sank down.
rows.reference: "I heard my wife cry for help, but then silence.

rows.source: Mí ò mọ ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ sí ìyàwó àti ọmọ mi
rows.output: I don't know what happened to my wife and children
rows.reference: I don't know what happened to her and my child.

rows.source: Mo ní ìrètí pé kò sí ohunkóhun tó ṣe wọ́n”
rows.output: I hope that nothing bad happens to him."
rows.reference: I hope they are safe."

rows.source: Aṣojú ìjọba US ní orílẹ̀èdè China fẹ̀sùn kan orílẹ̀èdè náà pé ó ń ṣe ìpalára fún àwọn orílẹ̀èdè mìíràn pẹ̀lú pípolówó ẹ̀tàn.
rows.output: The US government's top trade envoy to China accused the country of undermining the global trade system with its "unfair" trade practices.
rows.reference: U.S. ambassador accuses China of 'bullying' with 'propaganda ads'

rows.source: Lẹ́yìn ọ̀sẹ̀ kan tí ìwé ìròyìn fún ìjọba China gbé ìròyìn olójúùwé mẹ́rin kan jáde nínú ìwé ìròyìn kan ní US. Ìròyìn náà ṣe àtòólẹ̀ àǹfààní tó wà láàrin òwò láàrin China àti US, èyí tí aṣojú ìjọba náà na ìka àbùkù kan China pé ó ń fi àwọn ìwé ìròyìn orílẹ̀èdè Amẹ́ríkà tan àwọn ènìyàn.
rows.output: After a week of newspaper coverage for the Chinese government published four opinion articles in a US newspaper, the report highlighted the benefits of trade between China and the US. The Chinese government's representative criticized the US for spreading Chinese propaganda.
rows.reference: A week after an official Chinese newspaper ran a four-page ad in a U.S. daily touting the mutual benefits of U.S.-China trade, the U.S. ambassador to China accused Beijing of using the American press to spread propaganda.

rows.source: U.S. Ààrẹ orílẹ̀èdè U.S. Donald Trump ní Ọjọ́rú tó kọjá tọ́ka sí ìròyìn tí China gbé jáde nínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register- ilé-iṣẹ́ ìwé ìròyìn tí ń tà jùlọ ní ìpínlẹ̀ Iowa fẹ̀sùn kan China pé ó ń gbìyànjú láti dásí ètò ìdìbò ilé fún ilé amòfin tí yóò wáyé ní ọjọ́ kẹfà oṣù kọọkànlá. Orílẹ̀èdè China kọ̀ jálẹ̀ pé àwọn kò mọwọ́-mẹsẹ̀ nípa ẹ̀sùn náà.
rows.output: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday accused China of trying to interfere in the U.S. presidential election scheduled for November 6. China has denied the allegations.
rows.reference: U.S. President Donald Trump last Wednesday referred to the China Daily's paid supplement in the Des Moines Register - the state of Iowa's biggest selling newspaper - after accusing China of seeking to meddle in the Nov. 6 U.S. congressional elections, a charge China denies.

rows.source: Ibu ẹnu atẹlu Trump ti Beijing n gbiyanju lati dasi ninu idibo U.S saami si ohun ti awọn osisẹ U.S sọ fun Reuters jẹ ipele tuntun ninu irusoke ipolongo ibo lọdọ Washington lati funmọ China.
rows.output: Trump's trade war with Beijing is trying to drag the U.S. into a new phase of the election campaign, according to something that U.S. officials told Reuters is a new level of escalation in the trade war with Washington.
rows.reference: Trump's accusation that Beijing was trying to meddle in U.S. elections marked what U.S. officials told Reuters was a new phase in an escalating campaign by Washington to put pressure on China.

rows.source: Bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ kìí ṣe ohun àràmọ̀ndà kí àwọn ìjọba òkèèrè ṣe ìpolówó fún ìlọsíwájú ọrọ̀ ajé, rògbòdìyàn nípa ọrọ̀ ajé wà láàrin Beijing ati Washington, èyí tí ó sì fà á kí àwọn méjèèjì gbé owó lórí àwọn ọjà tí ó ń wọlé láti orílẹ̀èdè kejì.
rows.output: Although it is not a new thing for foreign governments to promote economic progress, there is a dispute between Beijing and Washington over economic issues, which has led both sides to impose tariffs on imports from the other country.
rows.reference: While it is normal for foreign governments to place advertisements to promote trade, Beijing and Washington are currently locked in an escalating trade war that has seen them level rounds of tariffs on each other's imports.

rows.source: Àwọn onímọ̀ lórílèedè U.S. wòye pé China ṣe àfikún owó lè ọjà tó ń wọlé sí U.S. láti orílẹ̀èdè China pàápàá jùlọ ní àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ bíi Iowa tí ó gbárùkù Trump àti ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú rẹ̀.
rows.output: US experts believe that China has added a large amount of currency to the US dollar inflow from China, especially in states like Iowa that Trump and his supporters have targeted.
rows.reference: China's retaliatory tariffs early in the trade war were designed to hit exporters in states such as Iowa that supported Trump's Republican Party, Chinese and U.S. experts have said.

rows.source: Aṣojú ìjọba U.S. ni China àti Gómìnà tẹ́lẹ̀ rí fún ìpínlẹ̀ Iowa, ẹni tí ó ń ta ohun ògbìn sí China jù, Terry Branstad sọ pé China ṣe ìpalára fún àwọn òṣìṣẹ́, okoòwò àti àgbẹ̀ nílẹ̀ Amẹ́ríkà.
rows.output: The U.S. Trade Representative to China and former Governor of Iowa, Terry Branstad, stated that China has harmed American workers, businesses, and farmers.
rows.reference: Terry Branstad, the U.S. ambassador to China and the former longtime governor of Iowa, a major exporter of agricultural goods to China, said Beijing had hurt American workers, farmers and businesses.

rows.source: Branstad wòye nínú ìwé tí ó kọ sínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register ní ọjọ́ Àìkú pé China ti sa gbogbo ipa wọn láti ṣe ìpolongo ẹ̀tàn nínú àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn ní Amẹ́ríkà.
rows.output: Branstad wrote in a column for the Des Moines Register on Sunday that China has used all its power to promote its propaganda in the media in the United States.
rows.reference: China, Branstad wrote in an opinion piece in Sunday's Des Moines Register, "is now doubling down on that bullying by running propaganda ads in our own free press."

rows.source: "Ìjọba China ń ṣe àmúlò ètò ìròyìn tí kò ní ìpalára láti ọ̀dọ̀ ìjọba tí ó wà ní Amẹ́ríkà láti sanwó ṣe ìpolongo ẹ̀tàn àti irọ́ nínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register,” ni ohun tí Branstad kọ.
rows.output: "China's authoritarian government is using a propaganda technique called 'information warfare' to spread false information and undermine democracy in the United States," Branstad wrote.
rows.reference: "In disseminating its propaganda, China's government is availing itself of America's cherished tradition of free speech and a free press by placing a paid advertisement in the Des Moines Register," Branstad wrote.

rows.source: "Ó tún tẹ̀síwájú pé “Lódì kejì ẹ̀wẹ̀, kò fi bẹ́ẹ̀ sí àwọn alátakò tàbí ààfihàn èrò àwọn ará China lórí irúfẹ́ ọwọ́ ti ìjọba fi mú ètò ọrọ̀ ajé. Èyí rí bẹ́ẹ̀ nítorí abẹ́ ìṣàkóso ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Chinese Communist Party ni àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn wà.
rows.output: He also continued that "Secondly, there is no such thing as the suppression of dissent or the suppression of the views of the Chinese people by the government. This is because under the rule of the Chinese Communist Party, the media are all under the control of the Party.
rows.reference: "In contrast, at the newsstand down the street here in Beijing, you will find limited dissenting voices and will not see any true reflection of the disparate opinions that the Chinese people may have on China's troubling economic trajectory, given that media is under the firm thumb of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.

rows.source: Ó tún fikún un pé ọ̀kan nínú àwọn ògbóntarìgì ilé ìwé ìròyìn ní orílẹ̀èdè China kọ̀ jálẹ̀ láti tẹ iṣẹ́ òun sínú ìwé ìròyìn wọn bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé Branstad kò dárúkọ ìwé ìròyìn náà ní pàtó.
rows.output: He also added that one of the top ten newspapers in China published an article from Branstad's book as a column in their newspaper without mentioning the book specifically.
rows.reference: He added that "one of China's most prominent newspapers dodged the offer to publish" his article, although he did not say which newspaper.

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ Ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì ń ya àwọn obìnrin kúrò pẹ̀lú ọ̀rọ̀ Kavanaugh, Àwọn Onímọ̀ kìlọ̀
rows.output: The Republican Party is split over Kavanaugh, Scientists warn
rows.reference: Republicans Alienating Women Voters Ahead of Midterms With Kavanaugh Debacle, Analysts Warn

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú bí ọ̀pọ̀ nínú àwọn àgbà ọ̀jẹ̀ olóṣèlú ẹgbẹ́ republican ṣe ń gbárùkù ẹni tí wọ́n yàn ní ilé ẹjọ́ tí ó ga jù lọ pẹ̀lú gbogbo àwọn ẹ̀sùn ìfipábóbìnrin lòpọ̀, àwọn onímọ̀ tí ń kìlọ̀ pé ọ̀rọ̀ yìí yóò lẹ́yìn pàápàá jùlọ láti ọwọ́ àwọn obìnrin nínú ètò ìdìbò áàrin táàmù.
rows.output: With so many Republican elders endorsing the top vote-getter in the primary, experts are warning that this trend will only continue, especially from women in the general election.
rows.reference: As many top Republicans stand-by and defend Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of several allegations of sexual assault, analyst have warned they will see a backlash, particularly from women, during the upcoming midterm elections.

rows.source: Ọ̀rọ̀ náà ti fa ọ̀pọ̀lọ̀pọ̀ rúkèrúdò, àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì sì ń takú àwọn yóò tún dìbò fún àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ wọn.
rows.output: The news has caused a stir in the political world, and the Republican Party is already looking for ways to regain control of the House.
rows.reference: The emotions surrounding this have been extremely high, and most Republicans are on record already showing they wanted to go forward with a vote.

rows.source: Ọ̀jọ̀gbọ́n nínú ẹ̀kọ́ ìṣèlú ní Maxwell School tí ó wà ní Yunifásítì Syracuse Grant Reheer ṣọ fún àwọn ìwé ìròyìn The Hill lọ́jọ́ Àbámẹ́ta pé ọ̀rọ̀ náà yóò lẹ́yìn.
rows.output: Professor of political science at the Maxwell School at Syracuse University Grant Reheer told the news outlet The Hill on Tuesday that the matter would follow.
rows.reference: Those things can't be walked back," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill for an article published Saturday.

rows.source: Reheer sọ pé òun kò rò bóyá ìgbésẹ̀ tí Amòfin Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) nípa pípè àjọ FBI láti wá ṣe ìwádìí àwọn ẹ̀sùn tí wọ́n fi kan Kavanaugh yóò tó láti pẹ̀tù sọ́kàn àwọn olùdìbò tí inú ń bí lọ́wọ́ lórí ọ̀rọ̀ náà.
rows.output: Reheer said he did not think that the actions of Senator Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) in calling the FBI to investigate the allegations against Kavanaugh would be enough to satisfy the concerns of voters who were already skeptical of the matter.
rows.reference: Reeher said he doubts Senator Jeff Flake's (R-Arizona) last-minute push for an FBI investigation will be enough to placate angry voters.

rows.source: "“Àwọn obìnrin ò ní gbàgbé ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ ní àná, wọn kò ní gbàgbé rẹ̀ lónìí, wọn kò sì ní gbàgbé rẹ̀ nínú ètò ìdìbò tí yóò wáyé ní oṣù kọọkànlá” ni ohun tí Karine Jean-Pierre, olùbádámọ̀ràn àgbà àti agbẹnusọ gbogbo fún ẹgbẹ́ MoveOn sọ lọ́jọ Ẹtì, èyí tí ó sì jẹyọ nínú ìwé ìròyìn Washington, D.C.
rows.output: "Women will not forget what happened yesterday, they will not forget it today, and they will not forget it in the elections that will take place in November" said Karine Jean-Pierre, the chief political correspondent and spokesperson for the group MoveOn, in a statement on Saturday, which was reported in the Washington Post.
rows.reference: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.

rows.source: Oṣù kọọkànlá ń bọ̀! Ní ohun tí àwọn afẹ̀hónúhàn ń ké bí wọ́n ṣe fi ìtaara wọn hàn ní ilé Aṣòfin pẹ̀lú bí àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì tí ó wà ní ìgbìmọ̀ tó ń ṣàkóso ọ̀rọ̀ ilé ẹjọ́ ṣe ń tẹ̀síwájú láti yan Kavanaugh sípò. The Mic jẹ́ kí ó yé wa pé èyí wáyé lẹ́yìn ẹ̀rí dọ́kítà Christine Blasey Ford. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic ní ó ń jọ́bọ̀ ìròyìn.
rows.output: November is coming! And what the protesters are screaming outside the Capitol with the Republican majority in the Senate continuing to push through Kavanaugh's nomination. The Mic makes it clear that this happened after the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reports, is a doctor.
rows.reference: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.

rows.source: Onímọ̀ ìṣèlú Stu Rothenberg sọ “Ìmọ̀sílára kò ní í sí lára àwọn ènìyàn, èyí yóò sì mú wọn dìbò”
rows.output: Political scientist Stu Rothenberg said "The public is not engaged, and that will affect turnout"
rows.reference: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.

rows.source: Àwọn ènìyàn tilẹ̀ ti ń sọ pé àwọn kò lè dúró kí ọjọ́ ìdìbò dé.
rows.output: People are already starting to talk about the election.
rows.reference: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.

rows.source: Ó ṣeéṣe kí ìmọ̀sílára pọ̀ sí pàápàá jùlọ láàrin àwọn obìnrin tí ó wà ní ìgbèríko àti àwọn ọmọbìnrin láàrin ọmọ ọdún méjìdínlógún sí óòkandínlọ́gbọ̀n tí wọ́n ò nífẹ̀ẹ́ ààrẹ, síbẹ̀ tí wọ́n kìí dìbò.”
rows.output: It is possible that the sense of entitlement is even greater among women in rural areas and among girls between the ages of 18 and 29 who do not want a president, but who do not vote.
rows.reference: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."

rows.source: Kí Ford tó jẹ́rìí ní gbangba nípa ẹ̀sùn ìfipábóbìnrin lòpọ̀ tí ó fi kan Kavanaugh ni àwọn onímọ̀ ti ń kìlọ̀ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí yíyan Kavanaugh sípò bu ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì lọ́wọ́.
rows.output: Before Ford confirmed publicly her allegations of sexual misconduct against Kavanaugh, experts were warning that Kavanaugh's selection could be a blow to the Republican Party.
rows.reference: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.

rows.source: “Ọ̀rọ̀ yìí ti dá yánpọyánrin kalẹ̀ fún ẹgbẹ́ wa” ni ohun tí Michael Steele tí ó fìgbà kan jẹ́ alága fún ìgbìmọ̀ gbogbogbò ní ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì sọ ní ọ̀sẹ̀ tó kọjá gẹ́gẹ́ bí NBC News ṣe sọ.
rows.output: "This phrase has been used to great effect by our side" is what Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, said last week according to NBC News.
rows.reference: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.

rows.source: “Ọ̀rọ̀ yìí kìí ṣe nípa bóyá àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì yan Kavanaugh sípò nìkan, ó tún nííṣe pẹ̀lú ọwọ́ tí ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì fi mú ọ̀rọ̀ náà àti ọwọ́ tí wọ́n fi mú Ford” Olùdarí ẹgbẹ́ tó ń ṣe ìrànlọ́wọ́ fún ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Dẹ́mókírààtì Priorities USA, Guy Cecil ló sọ èyí fún ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn náà.
rows.output: “This is not just about whether the Republican primary electorate chose Kavanaugh, it’s also about the hand that the Republican electorate gave to the nominee and the hand that the Republican electorate gave to Ford,” said Guy Cecil, the director of Priorities USA, a Democratic super PAC.
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Síbẹ̀, èrò àwọn ọmọ Amẹ́ríkà pín sí méjì lórí ọ̀rọ̀ náà pẹ̀lú bí wọn kò mọ ẹni tí ó yẹ kí wọ́n gbàgbọ́ nínú Kavanaugh àti Ford.
rows.output: However, public opinion in the US is divided on the matter, with many people unsure of who to believe.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Ìdìbò afèròhàn tí YouGov gbé kalẹ̀ fi hàn pé ìdá mọ́kànlelógoji nínú àwọn tó kópa nínú ètò ìdìbò náà sọ pé àwọn gba Ford gbọ́ nígbà tí ìdá márùndínlógójì ló sọ pé àwọn gba Kavanaugh gbọ́.
rows.output: The YouGov poll found that 51% of respondents said they had heard of Ford, while 60% said they had heard of Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Ìdá méjìdínlógójì ló sọ pé àwọn ní ìgbàgbọ́ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí Kavanaugh ti parọ́ nínú ẹ̀rí rẹ̀ nígbà tí ìdá ọgbọ̀n ló gbàgbọ́ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí Ford ti parọ́ nínú ẹ̀rí tirẹ̀ bákan náà.
rows.output: Eighty-two percent of those polled said they believed Kavanaugh lied under oath, while 30 percent said they believed Ford lied under oath as well.
rows.reference: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.

rows.source: The Guardian ròyìn pé lẹ́yìn tí amòfin Flake ké sí àjọ FBI, ìwádìí ti ń lọ lọ́wọ́ lórí ẹ̀sùn tí Ford and afẹ̀sùkan mìíràn Deborah Ramírez fi kan Kavanaugh.
rows.output: The Guardian reported that after Senator Flake called the FBI, the investigation was continuing into the allegations against Ford and another accuser, Deborah Ramirez, against Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.

rows.source: Ford jẹ́rìí níwájú ìgbìmọ̀ tó ń rí sí ilé ẹjọ́ nílé Aṣòfin pé Kavanaugh mú ọtí yó, ó sì fipá bá òun lòpọ̀ nígbà tí òun pé ọmọ ọdún mẹ́tàdínlógún.
rows.output: Ford confirmed to the House Judiciary Committee that Kavanaugh had consumed alcohol, and he was physically assaulted by a 17-year-old boy.
rows.reference: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.

rows.source: Ramirez ṣàlàyé pé Kavanaugh ṣí nǹkan ọmọkùnrin rẹ̀ fún òun láti rí nígbà tí wọ́n ń dìjọ kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ní Yale. Èyí ṣẹlẹ̀ ni patí kan tí wọ́n lọ láàrin ọdún 1980 síwájú sí i.
rows.output: Ramirez explained that Kavanaugh exposed his penis to her during a study break at Yale. This occurred in a single instance between 1980 and 1982.

rows.source: The Dane fakọyọ ní ọdún 1997 ní Valderrama, níbití Seve Ballesteros ti ní àmì ayò márùn lórí akẹgbẹ́ wọn láti Amerika, ṣùgbọ́n ṣóńsó imú wọn ní wọ́n fí gbégbá orókè ní ìlà-ìparí tí wọ́n sì borí pẹ̀lú 14½-13½.
rows.output: The Dane was defeated in 1997 at Valderrama, where Seve Ballesteros had won five majors against his American counterpart, but they were denied a share of the spoils when they were disqualified for a rules breach on the final hole and lost 14½-13½.
rows.reference: The Dane made his debut in the 1997 match at Valderrama, where a side captained by Seve Ballesteros held a five-point advantage over the Americans but only just got over the finishing line with their noses in front by the narrowest of margins, winning 14½-13½.

rows.source: “Kí ó máa rán ara rẹ létí pé a gbégbá orókè ní Valderrama; a gbìyànjú Brookline bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé a fìdí rẹmi, ṣùgbọ́n ní Valderrama a bórí gíníngínín. Bjorn, sọ pé nígbàtí òun wó ìdíje àwọn kíílàsì 2018 bí wọ́n ṣe borí pẹ̀lú 5-3 ní ọjọ́ Furaide àti ní àná bí wọ́n ṣe borí Le Golf National pẹ̀lú 10-6.
rows.output: "Remember that we played the high course at Valderrama; we tried Brookline as much as we could, but at Valderrama we were the masters. Bjorn, said that when he played the 2018 class as they won with 5-3 on Friday and yesterday as they won Le Golf National with 10-6.
rows.reference: "You keep reminding yourself that we had a big lead at Valderrama; we had a big lead at Brookline, where we lost, and at Valderrama, where we won, but only just," said Bjorn, pictured, after watching the Class of 2018 win 5-3 both on Friday and yesterday to lead 10-6 at Le Golf National.

rows.source: Furyk funra ara rẹ ti wà ní apá méjèèjì ibi ti àwọn ọjọ́ tó kẹ́hìn ńlá ti ṣàdédé yípadà, lẹ́yìn tí ó ti jẹ́ ara àwọn alájọṣepọ̀tó tò borí ní kí ó tó parí rẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́bí aláìláṣeyọrí ní Yúrópù mú kí “Ìyànu ńlá ní Mẹ̀dínà” ti ara rẹ̀ jáde.
rows.output: Furyk himself has been on both sides of the great divide, having been part of the winning team before the end of the great struggle, and now part of the losing side in Europe, which has led to the emergence of "The Great Disappointment" of himself.

rows.source: Ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi tuntun ti Germany ti di sísún síwájú lẹ́ẹ̀kan síi
rows.output: Germany's new naval ship has been delayed again
rows.reference: Germany's new warship postponed yet again

rows.source: Àkọ̀tun Ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi ti Jámáànù ní ó yẹ kí ó ti di fífi lọ́lẹ̀ ní ọdún 2014 láti pààrọ̀ àwọn ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi Sáà-ogún Dúkùú, ṣùgbọ́n kò ní rí bẹ́ẹ̀ títí di, ó kéré jù, ọdún í ó ń bọ̀ nítorí àwọn èròjà tó ti bàjẹ̀ àti àwọn ìnáwò tó ti ṣarajọ, ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn abẹ́léni ó jábọ̀ rẹ̀.
rows.output: The German Navy's 2014 plan to replace the Saar Class 4 submarines was not implemented until, at the earliest, 2018 due to technical problems and budgetary constraints, which were reported by the domestic press.
rows.reference: German Navy's newest frigate should have been commissioned in 2014 to replace ageing Cold War-era warships, but it won't be there until at least the next year due to faulty systems and snowballing cost, local media reported.

rows.source: Síṣàfilọ́lẹ̀ "Rheinland-Pfalz," olórí ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi tí ìsọ̀rí fírígéètì Baden-Wuerttemberg tuntun nini, ni ó ti di sísún ṣíwájú títi di ìdájì àkọ́kọ́ ọdún 2019, gẹ́gẹ́bi ìwé ìròyìn Die Zeit ṣe sọ tí ọgá ológun kan sọ.
rows.output: The launch of "Rheinland-Pfalz," the new frigate of the Baden-Wuerttemberg class, has been accelerated and is expected to be completed before the end of 2019, according to a report in the newspaper Die Zeit, which quotes a military official.
rows.reference: Commissioning of the "Rheinland-Pfalz," the lead ship of the brand new Baden-Wuerttemberg-class frigates, has now been postponed until the first half of 2019, according to Die Zeit newspaper citing a military spokesman.

rows.source: Ó yẹ kí ọkọ̀ ojú omi nlá náà darapọ̀ ní 2014, ṣùgbọ̀n àwọn wàhálà ìṣòro lẹ́yìn ìfakalẹ̀ rẹ̀ ní ó mú kí ìgbẹ́kẹ́lé nínú itẹ̀síwájú àkànṣe iṣẹ́ náà já sófo.
rows.output: The large ship was supposed to be completed in 2014, but the problems following its launch led to a delay in the project's progress.
rows.reference: The vessel should have joined the Navy in 2014, but the troubling post-delivery issues plagued the fate of the ambitious project.

rows.source: Àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi ńlá mẹ́rin ti ìsọ̀rí Baden-Wuerttemberg tí Àwọn ọmọ ogún ojú omi sànwó fún ;áti 2007 máa wá gẹ́gẹ́bí arọ́pò sí ìṣọ̀rí àwọn fírígéétì Bremen.
rows.output: Four large Baden-Wuerttemberg-type ships with 20 crew members will replace the Bremen-type ships from 2007.
rows.reference: The four Baden-Wuerttemberg-class vessels the Navy ordered back in 2007 will come as replacement to the ageing Bremen-class frigates.

rows.source: Ó yé wá pé wọ́n máa ṣàfihàn Kanọ́ọ̀nù tó lágbara,ọ̀wọ́ àwọn mísáìlì aṣòdì-sí-bàálù àti aṣòdì-sí-ọkọ̀ orí omi àti àwọn ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ nǹka ìjagun mìíràn, bíi rédà, ínfúrárẹ́ẹ̀dì àti àwọn ìfọ́wọ́sí abáfẹfẹ́ṣiṣẹ́.
rows.output: We understand that they will feature a powerful cannon, a torpedo, and other advanced military technology, such as radar, infrared sensors, and guided missiles.
rows.reference: It is understood they will feature a powerful cannon, an array of anti-aircraft and anti-ship missiles as well as some stealth technologies, such as reduced radar, infrared and acoustic signatures.

rows.source: Àwọn ohun pàtàkì mìràn gẹ́gẹ́bí ìgbà ìṣàbójútó lóòrèkóòrè - p yẹ kó ṣeéṣe láti ṣàfillẹ̀ awọn fírígéètì fún bí ọdún méjì jìnnà sí ìbúdó \kọ ojú omi.
rows.output: Other important factors include the frequency of inspections - ideally, these should be done every two years at the port of entry.
rows.reference: Other important features include longer maintenance periods - it should be possible to deploy the newest frigates for up to two years away from home ports.

rows.source: Síbẹ̀síbẹ̀, ìdádúró gbogbo ìgbà túmọ̀ sí wípé àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi ìṣaajú - tí wọn sọ pé ó jẹ́ kí ilẹ̀ jámánì ní agbara ní òkè òkun - ti máa di èyí tí kò bá ìgbà mu mọ́ ní àkókò tí wọ́n bá wọ iṣẹ́. Die Zelt ló pe àkíyèsí yìí.
rows.output: However, the continuous stoppage meant that the previous generation of steamships - which were said to have given Germany naval superiority - would soon be obsolete at the time they were put into service. The Zelt called this attention.
rows.reference: However, continuous delays mean that the cutting-edge warships - said to allow Germany to project power overseas - will already become outdated by the time they enter service, Die Zeit notes.

rows.source: Fírígèètì F125 tí ó kùnà náà gba gogbo ìròyìn kan ní ọdún tó kọjá, nígbàtí Àwọn ọmọ ogun ojú omi kọ̀ jàlẹ̀ láti ṣafilọlẹ̀ ọkọ̀ ojú omi ńlá náà tí wọ́n sì dá a padà sí ìlé iṣẹ́ ọkọ̀ ojú omi Blohm & Voss ní Hamburb.
rows.output: The F125 frigate that sank was carrying all the information of the year, while the Navy SEALs launched a large ship and returned it to the Blohm & Voss shipyard in Hamburg.

rows.source: Èyí jẹ ìgbà àkọ́kọ́ tí Àwọn ọ́mọ ogun ojú omi máa dá ọkọ̀ ojú omi padà fún ilé iṣẹ́ ọkọ̀ ojú omi ṣiṣe lẹ́yìn tí wọn ti fà á kalẹ̀.
rows.output: This was the first time that the Navy had returned a ship to the Navy Yard for repair after it had been launched.
rows.reference: This was the first time the Navy has returned a ship to a shipbuilder after delivery.

rows.source: Díẹ̀ ní a mọ̀ nípa ìdí tí ọkọ̀ ojú omi náà fi di dídá padà, ṣùgbọ́n àwọn oníwè ìròyìn jámànù sọ díẹ nípa “àṣìṣe sọ́fútìwíà àti hádìwíà” tí ó mú kí ọkọ̀ ìfijagun ojú omi náà má wúlò tí ó bá di lílò ní ojú ogun.
rows.output: Some information is known about why the ship was sent back, but the press has reported little about the "software and hardware errors" that made the ship useless when used in combat.

rows.source: Àìpé sọ́fùtiwìà jẹ́ ohún tí ó ṣe pàtàkì gan nítorí awọn 120 awakọ̀ ojú omi ni wọ́n máa wa ìsọ̀rí ọkọ̀ ojú omi ńlá Baden-Wuerttemberg-class náà - èyí tí ó jẹ́ ìdájí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ nínú àwọn fírígéètì ìsọ̀rí Bremen àtijọ́.

rows.source: Bákan náà, ó ṣelẹ̀ pé ọkọ̀ ojú omi náà ti wúwo ju bí ó ṣe yẹ lọ èyí tí ó ṣàdínkù ìṣesí rẹ̀ tí ó sì mú ìdópín bá ìpa Àwọn ọmọ ogun ojú omi láti ṣàlékún àmúdágbà ọjọ́ iwájú.
rows.output: At the same time, the ship was also too heavy, which reduced its maneuverability and led to a collision with the naval forces, which damaged the future of the project.

rows.output: Attorney Christian Schertz stated that the ball would require the right to be recognized as a person in the proportion that the recognition of the right to be recognized as a person, which is a fundamental human right that has been recognized in recent years.

rows.source: Lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n ti padé ní pátí alẹ́, Ronaldao àti Mayorga ní wọ́n jábọ̀ pé wọn padà sí yàrá agbábọ̀ọ̀lù náà., níbi tí wọn ti fé ẹ̀sùn tí kò tíì lẹ́rìí k[sn pé ó fi ìpa báá a lòpọ̀ láti fùrọ̀, gẹ́gẹ́bí àkọ̀sílẹ̀ ìwé tí wọ̀n kọ ní Ilé ẹjọ Agbègbe Clark ní́ Nevada.

rows.source: Brexit: UK ‘má kábámọ̀ títí ayé’ nípa pípàdńu àwọn àṣemọ́tò
rows.output: Brexit: UK 'will never be the same again' after losing single market status
rows.reference: Brexit: UK 'would forever regret' losing carmakers

rows.source: Orílẹ̀ èdè UK "má kábámọ̀ títí ayé" tí ó bá sọ ipò rẹ̀ nù bíi olórí lágbàáyé nínú mọ́tò ṣiṣẹ́ lẹ́yìn Brexit, àkswé fún okòòwò Greg Clark ló sọ bẹ́ẹ.
rows.output: The UK "will not be embarrassed until the end of time" if it fails to become the world's leading car manufacturer after Brexit, said Greg Clark, the business secretary.
rows.reference: The UK "would regret it forever" if it lost its status as a world leader in car manufacturing after Brexit, Business Secretary Greg Clark has said.

rows.source: Ótún sọ síwájú pé “nípa” pé Toyota UK ti sọ fún BBC pé tí Bírítéénì bá fi EU sílẹ̀ láì ní àdéhùn ìsòwò tó só pọ̀, ó máa ṣe ìdádúró ìgbéjáde-iṣẹ̀ ní ilé iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ ní Burnaston, ní ẹ̀bá Derby.
rows.output: Furthermore, it was reported by Toyota UK to the BBC that if Britain leaves the EU without a trade agreement, it will also halt production at its Burnaston plant, east of Derby.
rows.reference: He added it was "concerning" that Toyota UK had told the BBC that if Britain left the EU without a deal it would temporarily halt production at its factory in Burnaston, near Derby.

rows.source: "A nílò àdéhùn ìṣòwò,” Ọ̀gbẹ́ni Clark ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: "We need to make a trade," Mr. Clark said.
rows.reference: "We need a deal," Mr Clark said.

rows.source: Aṣemọ́tò Jàpáàanù sọ pé ipa ààlà máa ṣe ìdádúró tí ó bá lọ jẹ́ pé kò sí àd’hpùn ìṣòwò Brexit lẹ́ mú kí ìpàdánù iṣẹ́ wà.
rows.output: The Customs Union said that the impact of the border would be that there would be no Brexit trade deal.

rows.source: Ẹ̀rọ̀ iṣẹ́ Burnaston - tí ó ń ṣe Toyota Auris àti Avensis - pèsè mọ́tò tó súnmọ́ 150,000 ní ọdún tó kọjá tí ó sì jẹ́ pé 90% ní wọ́n ṣàgbéjáde sí Ìṣọ̀kan Yúròpù tó kù.
rows.output: The Burnaston plant - which produces the Toyota Auris and Avensis - manufactures approximately 150,000 vehicles per year and is 90% exported to the rest of Europe.
rows.reference: The Burnaston plant - which makes Toyota's Auris and Avensis - produced nearly 150,000 cars last year of which 90% were exported to the rest of the European Union.

rows.source: "Ìwòyé mi ni pé tí Bírítéènì ba fi le jáde kúrò ní EU láìròtẹ́lẹ̀ ní òpin oṣù kẹta, ìgbéjáde máa dúró ní ilé iṣẹ́ wa,” Marvi Cooke ni ó sọ bẹ́ẹ̀, Alákòóso adarí ní Burnaston.
rows.output: "My view is that if Britain leaves the EU unceremoniously at the end of March, then production will stop at our plant," said Marvi Cooke, managing director at Burnaston.
rows.reference: "My view is that if Britain crashes out of the EU at the end of March we will see production stops in our factory," said Marvin Cooke, Toyota's managing director at Burnaston.

rows.source: Àwọn aṣemọ́tò UK tí fi ìjayà wọn hàn nípa fífi EU sílẹ̀ láìní àdéhùn lórí bí kíkọjá láàlà òkòwò ṣe máa ṣiṣẹ́, gẹ́gẹ́bí i Honda, BMW àti Jaguar Land Rover.
rows.output: UK carmakers who were so excited to ditch the EU without a deal on how to regulate the auto industry, as Honda, BMW and Jaguar Land Rover.
rows.reference: Other UK car manufacturers have raised fears about leaving the EU without agreement on how cross-border trade will function, including Honda, BMW and Jaguar Land Rover.

rows.source: BMW, fún àpẹẹrẹ, sọ pé ò máa ti Ẹ̀rọ iṣẹ́ kékeré rẹ̀ ní Oxford fún oṣù kan tí ó tẹ̀lé Brexit.
rows.output: For example, BMW said it would temporarily close its Mini plant in Oxford for a month following Brexit.
rows.reference: BMW, for example, says it will close its Mini plant in Oxford for a month following Brexit.

rows.source: Ohun ìkọminú jùlọ jẹ́mọ́ ohun tí àwọn aṣemọ́tò sọ pé ọ jẹ àwọń èwu ètò ìpèsè tí ó bá ṣẹlẹ̀ pé kò sí àdéhun ìṣòwò Brexit.
rows.output: The most alarming thing is what the technocrats say: that you are a threat to the supply chain that would occur in the event of a no-deal Brexit.

rows.source: Ìgbéjáde àtòpọ̀ Toyota dá lórí i “tó bá àkókò mu”, pẹ̀lú àwọn ẹ̀yà ara rẹ̀ tí ó ń wọlé ní gbogbo ìṣẹ́jú 37 láti ọ̀dọ̀ olùgbéjáde wọn ní UK àti EU fún àwọn mọ́tò láti tà jáde.
rows.output: The launch of Toyota's new model is based on "just-in-time" principles, with its parts arriving every 37 seconds from its UK and EU factories for vehicles to be shipped out.

rows.source: Tí UK bá fi EU sílẹ̀ láìsí àdéhùn ìṣòwò ní 29 oṣù kẹta, ìdíwọ́ le wà ní ààlà ibode tí àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ sọ pé o le já sí ìdádúro àti àìnító àwọn ẹ̀yà ara.
rows.output: If the UK leaves the EU without a trade deal on 29 March, there could be a hard border on the island of Ireland. This would be a serious problem, as it would create a barrier to trade and movement between Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.

rows.source: Kò ní ṣeéṣe fún Tòyótà láti ní ọjà nílẹ̀ tó ju ìwọ̀n ọjọ́ kan lọ ní ibi Ẹ̀rọ iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ ní Derbyshire, ilé iṣẹ́ náà ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀, àtipé ìgbéṣẹ́jáde máa dáwọ́ dúró.

rows.source: Mr Clark sọ pé ète Theresa May fún ìbáṣepọ̀ ọjọ́ iwájú pẹ̀lú EU jẹ́ “àmọ̀ǹmọ̀ṣe láti yàgò fún àwọn àyẹ́wò ní ààlà ìbodè náà.”

rows.source: "A nílò láti ní àdéhùn ìṣòwò. A nílò láti ní àdéhùn ìṣòwò tó dára jùlọ tí ó máa gbà wá láàyè bí mo ṣe sọ, tí kò kì í ṣe àṣeyọrí nìkán ní àkókò yì tí a lé gbàdún, ṣùgbọ́n fún wa láti má le sọ àǹfààní yìí nù,” ó sọ fún ètò rédíò 4 BBC Lónìí bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: "We need to have a trade agreement. We need to have the best trade agreement that will allow us to be as I said, not just a success in this time, but for us not to lose this opportunity," he told BBC Radio 4 Today.
rows.reference: "We need to have a deal. We want to have the best deal that will allow as I say not just the success at present to be enjoyed but for us to grasp this opportunity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

rows.source: "Ẹ̀rí àrídájú tí kìíṣe láti ọ̀dọ̀ Toyotà nìkan ṣùgbọ́n tí ó jẹ́ ti àwọn àṣemọ́tò jáde míràn ní pé a nílò láti rí dájú pé a tẹ̀síwájú nínú ohun tí a ti ńṣe láṣeyọrílórí àwọn ààtò ìpèsè.”
rows.output: "Concrete evidence not only from Toyota but also from other automakers is that we need to ensure that we continue on the path we have been on with regard to procurement plans."
rows.reference: "The evidence from not just Toyota but other manufacturers is that we need to absolutely be able to continue what has been a highly successful set of supply chains."

rows.source: Toyota kò le sọ pàtò bí ó ṣe máa pẹ́ tó kí ìgbéṣẹ́jáde tó le dáwọ́ dúró, ṣùgbọ́n nígbà tí ó bá ṣe díẹ̀, ó kìlọ̀ pé àwọn ìṣùnà mìràn tó le jẹyọ máa ṣàdínkù ìledíje ẹ̀rọ ìṣẹ́ tí ó sì máa jásí ìpàdánù iṣẹ́.
rows.output: Toyota cannot predict when the current shortage of semiconductor chips will end, but when it does, it warns that other shortages may arise that will reduce the production of automotive electronics and lead to job losses.
rows.reference: Toyota was unable to say how long production would be stopped, but in the longer term, warned that added costs would reduce the plant's competitiveness and eventually cost jobs.

rows.source: Ìpàdé Trump pẹ̀lú Rosenstein lé ní ìdádúró lẹ́ẹ̀kan síi, Ilé Funfun Báláu ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: The Trump-Rosenstein meeting was delayed again, according to White House Balcony.

rows.source: Ìpàdé onípinnu-ńlá Donald Trump pẹ̀lú ìgbákejì àṣòfin gbogbogbò Rod Rosenstein le “sún síwájú fún ọ̀ṣẹ̀ kan mìíràn” bí ìjà lórí ẹnítí wọn dábàá fún ilé ẹjọ́ gíga Brett kavanaugh ṣe tẹ́ ṣíwájú, Ilé Funfun Báláú ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀ ní Ọjọ́ ìsinmi.
rows.output: The Trump-Rosenstein meeting could be delayed for another week or so as the battle over the Trump nominee for the Supreme Court, Brett Kavanaugh, has advanced, White House officials said on Sunday.
rows.reference: Donald Trump's high-stakes meeting with deputy attorney general Rod Rosenstein could be "pushed back another week" as the fight over supreme court nominee Brett Kavanaugh continues, the White House said on Sunday.

rows.source: Rosensteinní ó ń ṣàbójútó iṣẹ́ àgbẹjọ́rò pàtàkì Robert Mueller, tí ó ń ṣe ìwádìí lórí i ìkọlù Rọ́ṣíà lórí ìdìbò, ìbáṣepọ̀ láàrin àwọn òṣiṣẹ́ Trump àti Rọ́ṣíà àti bí ó ṣe ṣẹéṣe sí fún ààrẹ láti dènà ètò ìdájọ tó péye.
rows.output: Rosenstein oversees the work of special counsel Robert Mueller, who is investigating Russian interference in the 2016 election, potential collusion between Trump associates and Russia, and whether Trump obstructed the investigation.
rows.reference: Rosenstein oversees the work of special counsel Robert Mueller, who is investigating Russian election interference, links between Trump aides and Russia and potential obstruction of justice by the president.

rows.source: Bóyá Trump máa dá igbákejì àṣòfin gbogbogbò dúró tàbí kò ní ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀, tí ó máa wá mú kí òmínira Mueller níra, ti jẹ́ kí Washington ṣòfófo fú ọ̀pọ̀ oṣù ṣẹ́yìn.
rows.output: Whether Trump fires Mueller or not, the investigation is likely to continue for many more months.
rows.reference: Whether or not Trump will fire the deputy attorney general, and thereby endanger Mueller's independence, has fuelled Washington gossip for months.

rows.source: Ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ oṣù yìí, ìwé ìròyìn New York Times jábọ̀ pé Rosenstein jíròrò lórí i pé oùn fẹ́ fí wáyà sára láti ṣe àkásílẹ̀ ìtàkurọ̀sọ pẹ̀lú Trump àti ìṣeéṣesí láti yọ ààrẹ nínú àtúnṣe 25.
rows.output: In the early part of this month, the New York Times reported that Rosenstein discussed the possibility of wearing a wire to record Trump and exploring the possibility of removing him from office under section 25.
rows.reference: Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that Rosenstein discussed wearing a wire to record conversations with Trump and the possibility of removing the president via the 25th amendment.
