rows.source: “Ọ bụghị naanị maka ntuli aka ndị ọgbakọ ma ọ bụ maka ntuli aka ikpeazụ ma ọ bụ ma etinyere Kavanaugh n’oche, ọ bụkwa maka otu ndị Repọblikan siri jikwaa ihe a ma ka ha siri meso ya omume,” Guy Cecil, onye isi Priorities USA, otu na-enyere aka ahọpụta ndị Demokrat, rụtụrụ ndị akụkọ aka.
rows.output: “It’s not just about the primary elections or the final election or whether Kavanaugh gets on the court, it’s also about how the Republicans are handling this and how they’re going to go about it,” said Guy Cecil, president of Priorities USA, a group that helps elect Democrats.
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, Ndị America dị ka ndị kewara ekewa n’onye ha ga-ekwenyere na ndapụta nkwuputa Ford na Kavanaugh, ebe ndị karịrị kwụnyere onye nke ikpeazụ.
rows.output: However, Americans are divided on whom they would support in a Ford-Kavanaugh ticket, with more than half supporting the latter.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Nyocha ọhụrụ sitere na YouGov gosiri na pesentị 41 ndị zara ajụjụ kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ nkwuputa Ford, ebe pesentị 35 kwuru na ha kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ Kavanaugh.
rows.output: A new study from YouGov found that 41% of respondents either strongly agree or somewhat agree with Ford's allegations, while 35% said they either strongly agree or somewhat agree with Kavanaugh's denial.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Na mgbakwunye, pesentị 38 kwuru na ha chere na Kavanaugh eleghị anya sịrị asị ma ọ bụ sịa asị kpamkpam n’oge nkwuputa ya, ebe naanị pesentị 30 kwuru otu ihe ahụ maka Ford.
rows.output: In addition, 38 percent said they believed Kavanaugh was probably or definitely lying during his testimony, while only 30 percent said the same about Ford.
rows.reference: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.

rows.source: Ka Flake mechara nkwanye, ndị FBI na-eme nyocha ugbu a n’ebubo Ford boro, yana opekempe otu onye ebubo ọzọ, Deborah Ramirez mere, The Guardian kwuputara.
rows.output: After Flake's acquittal, the FBI is currently investigating Ford's allegations, as well as at least one other allegation, by Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.
rows.reference: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.

rows.source: Ford mere nkwuputa n’ihu Ọgbakọ Ndị Ikpe Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu n’okpuru iyi n’izu gara aga na Kavanaugh dakporo ya n’anya mmanya mgbe ọ gbara afọ 17.
rows.output: Ford made a statement in front of the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh assaulted her in an intoxicated state when she was 17 years old.
rows.reference: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.

rows.source: Ramirez boro ebubo n’onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu ahụ gosiri ya ike ya mgbe ha na-eme ọgbakọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ n’oge ha na-agụ akwụkwọ na Yale n’ime 1980s.
rows.output: Ramirez accused the nominee to the Supreme Court of showing her his muscles during a dinner meeting while they were students at Yale in the 1980s.
rows.reference: Ramirez alleges that the Supreme Court nominee exposed his genitals to her while they attended a party during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.

rows.source: Onye Mmepụta World Wide Web Na-ama Atụmatụ Ịmalite Ịntanetị Ọhụrụ Iji Sonyere Google na Facebook

rows.source: Tim Berners-Lee, onye mmepụta World Wide Web, na-amalite ụlọ ọrụ ọhụrụ nke ga-achụso Facebook, Amazon na Google.
rows.output: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is starting a new company that will compete with Facebook, Amazon, and Google.
rows.reference: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a startup that seeks to rival Facebook, Amazon and Google.

rows.source: Atụmatụ ọhụrụ ahụ nke ọkaibe teknụzụ, Inrupt, bụ ụlọ ọrụ na-agbakwasa ụkwụ na ngwanro ghe oghe Berners-Lee, Solid.
rows.output: The new plan by the technology expert, Inrupt, is a company that is expanding on Berners-Lee's open-source software, Solid.
rows.reference: The technology legend's latest project, Inrupt, is a company that builds off of Berners-Lee's open source platform Solid.

rows.source: Solid na-enye ndị ọrụ oghere ịhọrọ ebe ha ga-echekwa data ha yana ozi ndị mmadụ nwere ike nweta.
rows.output: Solid provides users with the opportunity to choose where they will store their data and the information that people can access.
rows.reference: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.

rows.source: N’ajụjụ ọnụ pụrụ iche Fast Company mere, Berners-Lee mara njakịrị na ebumnuche ejiri mebe Inrupt bụ “ịchị mba ụwa.”
rows.output: In a special interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the purpose of Inrupt was "to take over the world."
rows.reference: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."

rows.source: “Anyị ga-eme ya ugbu a,” o kwuru maka ụlọ ọhụrụ ahụ.
rows.output: "We're going to make a new one," she said.

rows.source: “Ọ bụ oge a ga-edebanye na akụkọ.”
rows.output: "It's time to make history."

rows.output: The device uses Solid State Technology to enable people to create "personal offline data storage" or POD.
rows.reference: The app uses Solid's technology to allow people to create their own "personal online data store" or a POD.

rows.source: Ọ nwere ike inwe ndepụta kọntaktị, ndepụta ihe omume, kalenda, ọba egwu yana ngwa nkeonwe na nke eji arụ ọrụ.
rows.output: It can have a contact list, a to-do list, a calendar, a music library, and a collection of notes and memos.

rows.output: It's like having Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, and Spotify all in one search bar, all at once.

rows.source: Ihe pụrụ iche na ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị bụ na ọ dịịrị naanị onye ji ya arụ ọrụ ịhọrọ onye ga-enweta ozi nke ọ bụla.
rows.output: The unique thing about private data storage on the internet is that it is up to the person who uses it to choose who gets to access their information.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ na-akpọ ya “ikike nkeonwe site na data.”
rows.output: The company calls it "personal privacy from data."

rows.source: Ebumnuche Inrupt, dabere na CEO John Bruce, bụ ka ụlọ ọrụ kpokọba, akụrụngwa, usoro na nka dabara daba iji nyere aka mee ka Solid rute onye ọ bụla.
rows.output: Inrupt's goal, based on CEO John Bruce, is to bring together a network, resources, systems, and art to help make Solid accessible to everyone.
rows.reference: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ nwere naanị Berners-Lee, Bruce, ebe nchekwa IBM zụtara na ya, ndị ọrụ nrụpụta ewere n’ọrụ ịrụ n’atụmatụ ahụ yana ọgbakọ ndị koodu wepụtara onwe ha.
rows.output: The company had only Berners-Lee, Bruce, and a few IBM employees who were taken on to work on the project, as well as a group of volunteer coders.

rows.source: Site n’izu a, ndị nrụpụta teknụzụ ụwa gbaa gburugburu ga-enwe ike mebe ngwa agaghị ekpokọba ọnụ nke ha site n’iji ngwa mebere na websaịtị Inrupt.
rows.output: From today, global technology manufacturers will be able to create non-removable applications using the Inrupt-made applications on the Inrupt website.

rows.source: Berners-Lee kwuru na ya ndị otu ya anaghị agwa ndị “Facebook na Google okwu banyere ma ha a ga-amalite ma ọ bụ hapụ mmalite mgbanwe kpamkpam ebe ụdịdị azụmahịa na-atụgharị ozugbo na ntabi anya.
rows.output: Berners-Lee said that his team was not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether they would start or stop the beginning of a fundamental change in the business model that is immediately turning into a commercial model."
rows.reference: Berners-Lee said that he and his team are not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether or not to introduce a complete change where all their business models are completely upended overnight.

rows.source: “Anyị anaghị anata ha ikike.”
rows.output: “We are not here to receive them.”

rows.source: Na mbipụta emere na Medium na Satọde, Berners-Lee dere na “ebumnuche Inrupt bụ inye ike azụmahịa na gburugburu inyere aka chekwaa ntụkwasị obi na ịdị mma weebu ọhụrụ ahụ arụrụ na Solid.”
rows.output: In a Medium post published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that "Inrupt's goal is to give power to the businesses and the environment that help to keep trust and integrity in the new web that we are building on Solid."
rows.reference: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that Inrupt's "mission is to provide commercial energy and an ecosystem to help protect the integrity and quality of the new web built on Solid."

rows.source: Na 1994, Berners-Lee gbanwere Ịntanetị mgbe ọ mepụtara World Wide Web Consortuim na Massachusetts Institue of Technology.
rows.output: In 1994, Berners-Lee revolutionized the Internet by creating the World Wide Web Consortium at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

rows.source: N’ọnwa ndị adịbeghị anya, Berners-Lee bụ olu na-ada ụda na arụmarụ ụka nnwere onwe ọrụ ịntanetị.
rows.output: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been a vocal advocate for internet freedom.
rows.reference: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been an influential voice in the net neutrality debate.

rows.source: Ọbulagodi mgbe a na-ebuputa Inrupt, Berners-Lee ga-anọrọ dịka onye Mmepụta na Onye Isi nke World Wide Web Consortuim, Web Foundation na Open Data Institute.
rows.output: Even after the departure of Inrupt, Berners-Lee would remain as the Inventor and Chief Architect of the World Wide Web Consortium, the Web Foundation, and the Open Data Institute.

rows.source: “A na m enwe olile anya nke ukwuu maka oge na-abịa n’ihu nke weebu,” Berners-Lee gbakwunyere.
rows.output: "I'm very excited about the future of the web," Berners-Lee added.
rows.reference: "I'm incredibly optimistic for this next era of the web," Berners-Lee added.

rows.output: Ronaldo is seeking to join Real Madrid from Manchester United during the summer transfer window, and in the current heat, he has moved to a major Italian club, Juve, on a €100 million contract.
rows.reference: Ronaldo was on the verge of joining Real Madrid from Manchester United at the time of the alleged assault, and this summer moved to Italian giants Juve in a €100 million deal.

rows.source: Brexit: UK “ga na-enwe nwute dịrị gaba ma ndị na-arụ ụgbọ ala funari ha
rows.output: Brexit: UK "will regret" hard Brexit, car industry warns
rows.reference: Brexit: UK 'would forever regret' losing carmakers

rows.source: UK “ga-enwe nwute dịịrị gaba” ma ọ bụrụ na o tufuo ọkwa ya dị ka onye ọchịchị n’ịrụpụta ụgbọ ala n’ụwa ma Brexit gachaa, Ọde Akwụkwọ Azụmahịa Greg Clark kwuru.
rows.output: The UK "will be disappointed" if it loses its position as the world's leading car manufacturer after Brexit, said Business Secretary Greg Clark.
rows.reference: The UK "would regret it forever" if it lost its status as a world leader in car manufacturing after Brexit, Business Secretary Greg Clark has said.

rows.source: Ọ gbakwunyere na ọ bụ ihe “na-atụ uche” na Toyota UK gwara BBC na ọ bụrụ na Britain apụọ na EU na-enweghị nkwekọrịta, na ha ga-akwụsị nwa oge ịrụpụta ihe n’ụlọ nrụpụta dị na Burnaston, n’akụkụ Derby.
rows.output: He added that it was "on the cards" and that Toyota UK told BBC that if Britain left the EU without a deal, they would temporarily stop producing cars at their factory in Burnaston, near Derby.
rows.reference: He added it was "concerning" that Toyota UK had told the BBC that if Britain left the EU without a deal it would temporarily halt production at its factory in Burnaston, near Derby.

rows.source: “Anyị chọrọ nkwekọrịta,” Mr Clark kwuru.
rows.output: "We need a contract," Mr. Clark said.
rows.reference: "We need a deal," Mr Clark said.

rows.source: Onye ọrụ ụgbọ ala nke Japan ahụ kwuru na ndapụta nke igbu oge n’oke ala ma ọ bụrụ na enweghị nkwekọrịta Brexit nwere ike napụ ọrụ.
rows.output: The Japanese truck driver said that the outcome of Brexit delays could deprive him of work.
rows.reference: The Japanese carmaker said the impact of border delays in the event of a no-deal Brexit could cost jobs.

rows.source: Ụlọ nrụpụta nke Burnaston - bụ nke na-arụpụta Toyota Auris na Avensis - rụpụtara ihe ruru ụgbọ ala 150,000 n’afọ gara aga nke ebupuru 90% ya na mba European Union ndị ọzọ.
rows.output: The Burnaston plant - which manufactures the Toyota Auris and Avensis - produced approximately 150,000 vehicles in the previous year, with 90% of them exported to other European Union countries.
rows.reference: The Burnaston plant - which makes Toyota's Auris and Avensis - produced nearly 150,000 cars last year of which 90% were exported to the rest of the European Union.

rows.source: “Echiche m bụ na ọ bụrụ na Britain apụọ na EU na ngwucha Maachị, anyị ga-ahụ na nrụpụta kwụsịrị n’ụlọ nrụpụta anyị” Marvin Cooke onye isi njikwa Toyota na Burnaston kwuru.
rows.output: "My view is that if Britain leaves the EU at the end of March, we will see production stop at our plants," said Marvin Cooke, managing director of Toyota in Burnaston.
rows.reference: "My view is that if Britain crashes out of the EU at the end of March we will see production stops in our factory," said Marvin Cooke, Toyota's managing director at Burnaston.

rows.source: Ndị ọzọ na-arụpụta ụgbọ ala na UK na-atụ egwu banyere ịhapụ EU na-enweghị nkwekọrịta ka azụmahịa na-agafe oke ala ga-esi rụọ ọrụ, tinyere Honda, BMW na Jaguar Land Rover.
rows.output: Other car manufacturers in the UK are concerned about leaving the EU without a deal, as they fear that trade across borders will not function properly, including Honda, BMW, and Jaguar Land Rover.
rows.reference: Other UK car manufacturers have raised fears about leaving the EU without agreement on how cross-border trade will function, including Honda, BMW and Jaguar Land Rover.

rows.source: BMW, maka ọmụmatụ, kwuru na ya ga-emechi Obere ụlọ nrụpụta ya dị na Oxford maka otu ọnwa ma emechaa Brexit.
rows.output: BMW, for example, has said that it will close its Mini plant in Oxford for a month after Brexit.
rows.reference: BMW, for example, says it will close its Mini plant in Oxford for a month following Brexit.

rows.source: Mkpatụta kacha gbasara ihe ndị na-arụ ụgbọ ala kwuru bụ n’ihe egwu mbunye ahịa ma ọ bụrụ na enwetaghị nkwekọrịta.
rows.output: The biggest concern was that it would be used to rip off consumers if the deal didn't go through.
rows.reference: The main concerns relate to what carmakers say are supply chain risks in the event of a no-deal Brexit.

rows.source: A na-eme nrụpụta na Toyota n’ahiri usoro “ọ bịa ozugbo”, ebe akụkụ ụgbọ ala na-eji nkeji 37 nwere esi n’aka ndị mbunye ahịa abịa, ma UK na EU maka ụgbọ ala atụrụ ahịa ya.
rows.output: The production is carried out in Toyota on the "just-in-time" process, where the parts of the vehicle take 37 minutes from the suppliers' arrival, and for the UK and EU for its own sales.
rows.reference: Toyota's production line is run on a "just-in-time" basis, with parts arriving every 37 minutes from suppliers in both the UK and the EU for cars made to order.

rows.source: Ọ bụrụ na UK ahapụ EU n’enwetaghị nkwekọrịta na Maachị 29, enwere ike inwe ọgbaghara n’oke ala bụ nke ụlọ nrụpụta kwuru na ọ nwere ike bute igbu oge yana ezughị ezu akụkụ ụgbọ ala.
rows.output: If the UK leaves the EU without a deal on March 29, there could be a shortage of parts that car manufacturers say could lead to delays and incomplete vehicles.
rows.reference: If the UK leaves the EU without a deal on 29 March, there could be disruption at the border which the industry says could lead to delays and shortages of parts.

rows.source: Ọ gaghị ekwe omume na Toyota ga-ahapụ ngwaahịa  karịrị nke otu ụbọchị n’ụlọ nrụpụta ha dị na Derbyshire, ụlọ ọrụ ahụ kwuru, yamere na nrụpụta ga-akwụsị.
rows.output: It would be impossible for Toyota to leave more than one day's worth of production at their Derbyshire factory, the company said, given that production would cease.
rows.reference: It would be impossible for Toyota to hold more than a day's worth of inventory at its Derbyshire plant, the company said, and so production would be stopped.

rows.source: Mr Clark kwuru na atụmatụ Chequers nke Theresa May maka mmekọrịta ha na EU n’ọdịnihu bụ “nke emebere ka ọ zenarị nyocha niile ahụ n’oke ala.”
rows.output: Mr. Clark said that Theresa May's Chequers plan for future relations with the EU was "designed to avoid all that scrutiny on the high ground."
rows.reference: Mr Clark said Theresa May's Chequers plan for future relations with the EU is "precisely calibrated to avoid those checks at the border."

rows.source: “Anyị chọrọ inwe nkwekọrịta.   Anyị chọrọ inwe nkwekọrịta kacha mma ga-enye anyị oghere dịka m na-ekwu, nke abụghị naanị inweta ọganihu ugbu a ma ka anyị jidekwa oghere a,” ọ gwara ihe mmemme BBC Radio 4 Today.
rows.output: "We want a deal.  We want the best deal that will give us the opportunity that I'm talking about, which is not just getting gains today but also keeping this opportunity," he told the BBC Radio 4 Today program.
rows.reference: "We need to have a deal. We want to have the best deal that will allow as I say not just the success at present to be enjoyed but for us to grasp this opportunity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

rows.source: “Akaebe sitere n’abụghị naanị Toyota ma ndị ọzọ na-eme nrụpụta bụ na ekwesịrị ịga n’ihu soro usoro mbunye ahịa nke na-aga nke ọma kpamkpam.”
rows.output: "Testimony from not only Toyota but also other manufacturers is that we need to continue with the successful purchasing process."
rows.reference: "The evidence from not just Toyota but other manufacturers is that we need to absolutely be able to continue what has been a highly successful set of supply chains."

rows.source: Toyota enweghị ike ikwu ogologo oge ole a ga-akwụsị ime nrụpụta, mana n’ote aka, ha na-adọ aka na ntị mgbakwunye ọnụego ga-ebelata ike asompi ya na emechaa a ga-anapụ ọrụ.
rows.output: Toyota cannot say how long the production stoppage will last, but on the one hand, they are warning of additional cost increases that will eventually weaken its competitiveness; on the other hand, they are indicating that the stoppage will be temporary.
rows.reference: Toyota was unable to say how long production would be stopped, but in the longer term, warned that added costs would reduce the plant's competitiveness and eventually cost jobs.

rows.source: Peter Tsouvallaris, bụ onye rụgoro ọrụ na Burnaston afọ 24, bụrụkwa onye nchịkọba otu ndị ọrụ n’ụlọ nrụpụta ahụ, kwuru na ndị otu ya na-atụ uche nke ukwuu: “N’ahụmihe m, ozugbo ọrụ ndị a lara, ha anaghị alaghachi azụ.
rows.output: Peter Tsouvallaris, who worked at Burnaston for 24 years, was the leader of a team of employees at the plant, said that his team was very concerned: "In my experience, once these jobs are gone, they are not coming back.
rows.reference: Peter Tsouvallaris, who has worked at Burnaston for 24 years and is the Unite union convenor at the plant, said his members are increasingly concerned: "In my experience once these jobs go they never come back.

rows.source: Otu onye nkwuchite okwu gọọmentị kwuru:  “Anyị eweputala atụmatụ doro anya were ntụkwasị obi maka mmekọrịta anyị na EU n’ọdịnihu.
rows.output: A government spokesperson stated: "We have put in place a clear and reliable plan for our future relations with the EU.
rows.reference: A government spokesperson said: "We have put forward a precise and credible plan for our future relationship with the EU."

rows.source: Enwere ike budaa oge nzụkọ Trump na Rosenstein ọzọ, White House kwuru
rows.output: The White House said that the Trump-Rosenstein meeting could be reopened.
rows.reference: Trump meeting with Rosenstein may be delayed again, says White House

rows.source: Enwere ike ibuda nzụkọ ahụ dị oke mkpa nke Donald Trump na osote onye isi ọka ikpe Rod Rosenstein nwere “izu ọzọ na-abịa” ebe mgba maka onye nhọpụta ụlọ ikpe kachasị elu Brett Kavanaugh na-aga n’ihu, White House kwuru na Sọnde.
rows.output: The crucial meeting between Donald Trump and Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein is "coming up in the next week" as the battle for the Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh continues, the White House said on Sunday.
rows.reference: Donald Trump's high-stakes meeting with deputy attorney general Rod Rosenstein could be "pushed back another week" as the fight over supreme court nominee Brett Kavanaugh continues, the White House said on Sunday.

rows.source: Rosenstein na-ahụ maka ọrụ pụrụ iche Robert Mueller bụ onye na-eme nyocha ntinye aka ndị Russia na ntuli aka, njikọ dị n’etiti ndị inyeaka Trump na Russia yana mgbachi nke inweta ikpe nkwumọtọ sitere na onye isi ala.
rows.output: Rosenstein oversees the special counsel Robert Mueller, who is investigating Russian interference in the election, the connections between Trump associates and Russia, and the counterintelligence investigation of the president.
rows.reference: Rosenstein oversees the work of special counsel Robert Mueller, who is investigating Russian election interference, links between Trump aides and Russia and potential obstruction of justice by the president.

rows.source: Ma Trump a ga-achụ ka ọ ga-ahapụ osote onye isi ọka ikpe ahụ, n’ihi ya tinye nnwere onwe Mueller n’ihe egwu, mụnyere ọkụ na asịrị Washington n’ọtụtụ ọnwa.
rows.output: But Trump is trying to force the resignation of the deputy chief justice, so he puts Mueller's independence at risk, lighting a fire in Washington for months.
rows.reference: Whether or not Trump will fire the deputy attorney general, and thereby endanger Mueller's independence, has fuelled Washington gossip for months.

rows.source: Na mbido ọnwa a, New York Times kwuputara na Rosenstein kwuru maka iyi eriri okwu iji dekọba nrụrịta ụka Trump na iwepu onye isi ala site n’ụzọ mmegharị 25th.
rows.output: In the beginning of this month, the New York Times reported that Rosenstein said he had considered wearing a wire to record Trump's conversations about removing the president from office through the 25th Amendment.
rows.reference: Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that Rosenstein discussed wearing a wire to record conversations with Trump and the possibility of removing the president via the 25th amendment.

rows.source: Rosenstein gọnarịrị akụkọ a.
rows.output: Rosenstein denied the report.
rows.reference: Rosenstein denied the report.

rows.source: Mana Mọnde gara aga ọ gara na White House, n’etiti mkpesa na ọ chọrọ irutu.
rows.output: But on Monday, he went to the White House, amid complaints that he wanted to get closer.
rows.reference: But last Monday he went to the White House, amid reports he was about to resign.

rows.source: Kama, ekwuputere nzụkọ n’etiti Trump, onye nke nọ na United Nations na New York maka Tọsde.
rows.output: Instead, a meeting was held between Trump, who was in the United Nations in New York for Thursday, and Kim.
rows.reference: Instead, a meeting with Trump, who was then at the United Nations in New York, was announced for Thursday.

rows.source: Trump kwuru na “ọ gaghị amasị” ya ịchụ Rosentein mana mgbe ahụ egbuturu oge nzụkọ ahụ iji zere ịkụkọta n’ọnụnụ ọgbakọ ndị ọkaikpe Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu nke Kavanaugh na otu n’ime ụmụ nwanyị ndị boro ya ebubo nke omume arụrụ ala, Dk Christine Blasey Ford, ha abụọ nyere akaebe.
rows.output: Trump said that "he would not like" to pursue Rosenstein but then delayed the meeting to avoid combining it with the confirmation hearing of Kavanaugh's Supreme Court nominee and one of the women who accused him of sexual misconduct, Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, who testified.
rows.reference: Trump said he would "prefer not" to fire Rosenstein but then the meeting was delayed to avoid a clash with the Senate judiciary committee hearing in which Kavanaugh and one of the women who have accused him of sexual misconduct, Dr Christine Blasey Ford, both testified.

rows.source: Na Fraịde, Trump tiri iwu nke nyocha FBI n’otu-izu maka ebubo chere Kavanaugh, nke gbukwuru oge nke ntuli aka Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu n’uju.
rows.output: On Friday, Trump ordered an FBI investigation into one-week allegations against Kavanaugh, which delayed the final vote of the Senate Committee on Confirmation.
rows.reference: On Friday, Trump ordered a one-week FBI investigation of claims against Kavanaugh, further delaying a full Senate vote.

rows.source: Ọdee Akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi nke Trump, Sarah Sanders, pụtara na Fox News na Sọnde.
rows.output: Trump's Press Secretary, Sarah Sanders, appeared on Fox News on Sunday.
rows.reference: Trump's press secretary, Sarah Sanders, appeared on Fox News Sunday.

rows.source: Ajụrụ ya maka nzụkọ Rosentein, o kwuru: “Atọọla ụbọchị maka nke ahụ, ọ nwere ike ịbụ n’izu na abịa, m na ahụ ka nke ahụ laghachiri otu izu n’ihi ihe niile na eme ugbu a na ụlọ ikpe kachasị n’obodo.
rows.output: He asked about the Rosentein meeting, and he said, "There's been a delay on that, it could be in the next week, I'm not sure, because of all the things going on right now in the Supreme Court."
rows.reference: Asked about the Rosenstein meeting, she said: "A date for that hasn't been set, it could be this week, I could see that pushing back another week given all of the other things that are going on with the supreme court.

rows.source: Mana anyị ga-ahụ, ọ na amasị m oge niile ịme ka ndị mgbasa ozi mara ihe na eme ozugbo.”
rows.output: But we'll see, I kind of like the feeling of getting the news out there right away."
rows.reference: But we'll see and I always like to keep the press updated."

rows.source: Ụfọdụ ndi nta akụkọ ga-adọkpụ ngozusike ahụ: Sanders emebeghị nchịkọta akụkọ nke White House kemgbe Septemba 10.
rows.output: Some journalists have been digging into the archives: Sanders has not compiled a record of White House press briefings since September 10.
rows.reference: Some reporters would contest that assertion: Sanders has not held a White House press briefing since 10 September.

rows.source: Onye nlekọta Chris Wallace jụrụ ihe kpatara ya.
rows.output: Chris Wallace's handler asked for an explanation.
rows.reference: Host Chris Wallace asked why.

rows.source: Sanders kwuru na ụkọ nchịkọta akụkọ bụ n’ihi nleda anya maka “nnukwu ọchụchọ nlebanye anya” nke ndị nta akụkọ TV,” agbanyeghi na o kwuru: “Agaghị m ekwenye n’ezie ha na ha na achọ oke nlebanye anya.”
rows.output: Sanders said the low ratings were due to "the high cost of the TV news business," despite saying: "I don't really believe they're really looking for that much coverage."
rows.reference: Sanders said the scarcity of briefings was not due to a distaste for TV reporters "grandstanding," although she said: "I won't disagree with the fact that they grandstand."

rows.source: Ọ tụnyere nkwukọrịta ozugbo n’etiti Trump na ndị mgbasa ozi ga-agbagote.
rows.output: He compared the immediate expectations between Trump and the media would exaggerate.
rows.reference: She then suggested direct contact between Trump and the press will increase.

rows.source: “Onye isi ala na enwe oge njụrịkọta ajụjụ ọnụ karịa onye isi ala ọ bụla bịara tupu ya,” o kwuru, tinye na arụtụghị aka n’ihe akaebe: “Anyị elenyela anya na nọmba ndị a.”
rows.output: “The president has had more press conferences than any president in history,” he said, adding that he didn’t point to any evidence: “We have seen the numbers.”
rows.reference: "The president does more Q&A sessions than any president has prior to him," she said, adding without citing evidence: "We've looked at those numbers."

rows.source: Nchịkọta akụkọ ga na eme, Sanders kwuru, mana “ọ bụrụ na ndị mgbasa ozi nwee ohere ịjụ onye isi ala nke United States ajụjụ ozugbo, nke ahụ ka ịgwa m okwu mma karịa.
rows.output: The summary of the story will be made, Sanders said, but "if the media have the opportunity to question the President of the United States immediately, that's what I'm telling you is better."
rows.reference: Briefings will still happen, Sanders said, but "if the press has the chance to ask the president of the United States questions directly, that's infinitely better than talking to me.

rows.source: Anyị na anwa ịme nke ahụ ọtụtụ oge, unu ahụla ka anyị mere nke ahụ n’izu ole ma ole gara aga, nke ahụ ga-anọchikwa nchịkọta akụkọ mgbe ị nwere ike ịgwa onye isi ala nke United States okwu.”
rows.output: We have been trying to do that for a while, you have seen us do that a few weeks ago, that would be the summary of the report when you can talk to the President of the United States."
rows.reference: We try to do that a lot and you've seen us do that a lot over the last few weeks and that's going to take the place of a press briefing when you can talk to the president of the United States."

rows.source: Trump kwa oge na aza ajụjụ mgbe ọ na ahapụ White House ma ọ bụ sonye n’oge njụajụjụ ma ọ bụ ọgbakọ ndị mgbasa ozi mgbe enwere ndị mbịambịa ndị ọchịchị.
rows.output: Trump often takes questions when leaving the White House or joining a press briefing when there are visiting officials present.
rows.reference: Trump regularly takes questions when leaving the White House or participating in open sessions or press conferences with visiting dignitaries.

rows.source: Ọgbakọ mgbasa ozi naanị ya anaghị adịkebe.
rows.output: A solo press conference is not common.
rows.reference: Solo press conferences are rare.

rows.source: Na New York n’izu a onye isi ala ikekwe kọwara ihe kpatara ya, na eme mpụta na adịghị mma, oge ụfọdụ mpụta jọrọ njọ n’ihu ndị nta akụkọ.
rows.output: In New York this week, the president may have explained why, in a series of public appearances, he sometimes looked terrible in front of the cameras.
rows.reference: In New York this week the president perhaps demonstrated why, making a freewheeling and at times bizarre appearance before gathered reporters.

rows.source: Ọde Akwụkwọ Ahụike degara ndị ọrụ EU akwụkwọ na NHS Scotland maka ihe egwu Brexit
rows.output: A letter from the Health Secretary to EU workers in NHS Scotland about Brexit risks
rows.reference: Health secretary writes to EU workers at NHS Scotland over Brexit fears

rows.source: Ọde Akwụkwọ Ahụike edegala akwụkwọ maka ndị ọrụ EU na arụ ọrụ na NHS nke Scotland iji gosi ekele nke obodo ahụ ma rịọ ka ha nọrọ mgbe Brexit gachara.
rows.output: The Health Secretary has written to EU nationals working in the NHS in Scotland to express the gratitude of the nation and request them to stay after Brexit.
rows.reference: The Health Secretary has written to EU staff working in Scotland's NHS to express the country's gratitude and wish for them to stay on post-Brexit.

rows.source: Jeane Freeman MSP zigara leta n’ime ọnwa isiii iji ruo mgbe ndị UK ga-apụ na EU.
rows.output: Jeane Freeman MSP sent a letter in March to reach out until the UK leaves the EU.
rows.reference: Jeane Freeman MSP sent a letter with less than six months to go until the UK withdraws from the EU.

rows.source: Gọọmentị ndị Scotland ewepụtala onwe ha iji kpuchie ụgwọ nke akwụkwọ anamachọihe ọkwa ndị bigoro n’obodo maka ndị amaala EU n’ọrụ ọhaneze ya ekewara ekewa.
rows.output: The Scottish Government has opted to cover the costs of residence permit applications for EU citizens in its devolved areas.
rows.reference: The Scottish Government has already committed to meet the cost of settled status applications for EU citizens working in its devolved public services.

rows.source: Na leta ya, Nwada Freeman dere: “N’oge ọkọchị, ụbụbọ n’etiti UK na EU na nsepụ aka agaala n’ihu, na aga irute mkpebi atụrụ anya n’ọtọm a.
rows.output: In her letter, Ms. Freeman wrote: "In the summer, the rift between the UK and the EU has continued to grow, and it is clear that the outcome of this dispute will be determined by the outcome of the election.
rows.reference: In her letter, Ms Freeman wrote: "Over the summer, negotiations between the UK and EU on withdrawal have continued, heading towards expected decisions this autumn.

rows.source: Mana Gọọmentị UK na ewelitekwa nkwadobe ya maka ọnọdụ enweghị nkwekọrịta ọ bụla.
rows.output: But the UK government is also preparing for a no-deal scenario.
rows.reference: But the UK Government has also been stepping up its preparations for a possible no-deal scenario.

rows.source: Ama m na nke a ga-abụ oge mgbakasị ahụ maka unu niille.
rows.output: I know this is going to be a lot of work for you, but I want you to know that I'm here for you.
rows.reference: I know this must be a very unsettling time for all of you.

rows.source: Ya kpatara m ji chọọ ikwuputegharị ugbu a nnukwu ugwu m na akwanyere ndị ọrụ niile maka enyemaka ha, agbanyeghị obodo ha.
rows.output: I am now determined to rebuild my strength and to help rebuild my country.
rows.reference: That is why I wanted to reiterate now how much I value the contribution of every member of staff, regardless of their nationality.

rows.source: Ndị ibe m si n’ofe EU, ma gafere, na eweta ahụmịhe na nka dị mkpa na agbatị ma melite ọrụ nke ọrụ ahụike, ma nyere ndị ọrịa na ogbe anyị na arụrụ ọrụ aka.
rows.output: My colleagues from the EU side, who passed through, brought valuable experience and skills to the work of the health sector, and helped the patients in our village.
rows.reference: Colleagues from across the EU, and beyond, bring valuable experience and skills that strengthen and improve the work of the health service, and benefit the patients and communities we serve.

rows.source: Scotland bụ be gị n’ezie, anyị chọrọ ka unu nọrọ ebe a.”
rows.output: Scotland is your home now, we want you to stay here.”

rows.source: Nancy Pelosi kpọrọ Brett Kavanaugh “isi mgbaka,” o kwuru na o tozughi iji rụọ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị
rows.output: Nancy Pelosi called Brett Kavanaugh "a threat to democracy," saying he is not fit to serve on the Supreme Court.

rows.source: Onye Ndu Ndị Ntakịrị N’ụlọ Nzụkọ Nancy Pelosi kpọrọ onye nhọpụta maka Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Kavanaugh “isi mgbaka” ma kwuo na ọ na ewe iwe ọkụ iji rụọ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị.
rows.output: House Speaker Nancy Pelosi called the Supreme Court nominee Kavanaugh "a nightmare" and said she was "fired up" to work with the Supreme Court.
rows.reference: House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi called Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh "hysterical" and said that he was temperamentally unfit to serve on the Supreme Court.

rows.source: Pelosi kwuru okwu ndị ahụ n’ajụjụ ọnụ na Satọde na Texas Tribune Festival na Austin, Texas.
rows.output: Pelosi made the comments in an interview at the Texas Tribune Festival in Austin, Texas.
rows.reference: Pelosi made the comments in an interview Saturday at the Texas Tribune Festival in Austin, Texas.

rows.source: “Enwenwughi m ike ịkwụsị ịche na ọ bụrụ na nwanyị mee ụdịrị ihe ahụ, ha ga-ekwu ‘isi mgbaka,”” Pelosi kwuru maka mmetụta ya n’ihe akaebe Kavanaugh n’ihu Ọgbakọ Ndị Ikpe nke Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu na Tọsde.
rows.output: "I can't help but think that if a woman had done the same thing, they would have said, 'That's okay, that's a woman's role,'" Pelosi said about her reaction to Kavanaugh's testimony before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Thursday.
rows.reference: "I couldn't help but think that if a woman had ever performed that way, they would say 'hysterical,'" Pelosi said about her reaction to Kavanaugh's testimony before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Thursday.

rows.source: Kavanaugh jiri nnukwu mwute gọnarị ebubo ndị ahụ na ọ wakporo Dk. Christine Blasey Ford n’ike mgbe ha abụọ bụ ndị ntorobịa.
rows.output: Kavanaugh vehemently denied the allegations of sexual misconduct with Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, a claim that was corroborated by multiple witnesses.
rows.reference: Kavanaugh emotionally denied allegations that he had sexually assaulted Dr. Christine Blasey Ford when they were both teenagers.

rows.source: N’oge nkwupute mmepe ya, mmụọ Kavanaugh di elu nke ukwuu, oge ụfọdụ ọ na achọ iti mkpu ma olu a na agbagbu ya ka ọ na ekwu maka ezinụlọ ya yana afọ ụlọ akwụkwọ kọleji ya.
rows.output: During his confirmation hearing, Kavanaugh's demeanor was notably high-strung, sometimes almost shrill, as he spoke of his family and his college years.
rows.reference: During his opening statement, Kavanaugh was very emotional, at times nearly shouting and choking up while discussing his family and his high school years.

rows.source: Ọ kọtọkwara ndị Demokrat nọ n’ọgbakọ ahụ n’ụzọ doro anya, na akpọ ebubo emere ya “mgbagbu omume dị egwu n’anya, akpara akpa” nke ndị mmesapụ ahụ na ewe iwe na Hillary Clinton dara na ntuli aka onye isi ala 2016 haziri.
rows.output: He also criticized the Democrats at the convention in a clear and direct manner, labeling the accusations made against him as "outrageous and disgusting" by the angry delegates who were angry at Hillary Clinton's defeat in the 2016 presidential election.
rows.reference: He also explicitly condemned Democrats on the committee, calling the allegations against him a "grotesque and coordinated character assassination" organized by liberals angry that Hillary Clinton lost the 2016 presidential election.

rows.source: Pelosi kwuru na ọ kwenyere na akaebe nke Kavanaugh gosiri ọ nweghị ike ịrụ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị, n’ihi o gosiri na ọ nweghị mmasị n’ebe ndị Demokrat nọ.
rows.output: Pelosi said that she believed the evidence against Kavanaugh showed that he could not work in the Supreme Court, because it showed that he had no interest in the Democrats.
rows.reference: Pelosi said that she believed Kavanaugh's testimony proved that he could not serve on the Supreme Court, because it showed that he is biased against Democrats.

rows.source: O kwuru “echere m na ọ kagburu onwe ya site na iji okwu ndị ahụ yana n’ụzọ o si kwutọọ Clintons yana ndị Demokrat,”
rows.output: He said "I think he's a self-destructing narcissist by using those words and the way he's talking about the Clintons and the Democrats,"
rows.reference: "I think that he disqualifies himself with those statements and the manner in which he went after the Clintons and the Democrats," she said.

rows.source: Pelosi dajụrụ mgbe ajụrụ ma ọ ga-achọ iwepu Kavanaugh ma ọ bụrụ na etinye ya n’oche, ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Demokrat nweta ọnụọgụgụ karịrị na Ụlọ nke Ndị Nnọchite.
